• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Abu Awana related to us, from Sulayman, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the Romans were defeated by the Persians, and the Muslims rejoiced at that. So God revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated...﴾ to the end of the verse."
• Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to us, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the Romans were overcome by the Persians, and this pleased the believers, because they were People of the Book. So God revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land﴾." He said: "They had been defeated before that, and then he recited until he reached ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the nearest land﴾:
I have already mentioned the view of some of them earlier, and I will mention the view of those whose view has not been mentioned.
• Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿in the nearest land﴾: he said, "It means: at the edge of Syria." The meaning of "adna" (nearest) is "aqrab" (closer), and it is the comparative form from "dunuww" and "qurb" (nearness). Its meaning is: "in the land nearest to Persia," and the mention of Persia was omitted because of what is indicated by the phrase ﴿in the nearest land﴾ concerning it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and they, after their defeat﴾:
It means: the Romans, after the Persians' defeat of them, will overcome the Persians.

* *

As for His words ﴿after their defeat﴾:
It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "ghalabtuhu ghalaba" (I overcame him with an overcoming), so the "ha'" (the feminine ending) was dropped from "ghalaba." It has also been said: "min ba'di ghalabihim" (after their defeat), and he did not say "min ba'di ghalabatihim" (after their defeat, with the feminine ending) because of the annexation (idafa), just as it was dropped in His words ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾ because of the annexation; the original phrase is "wa iqamat al-salah" (and the establishment of the prayer).
As for His words ﴿will overcome﴾ (sa-yaghlibun), all the readers agree on opening the "ya'" in it. According to the reading of one who reads ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been overcome﴾ with an opened "ghayn," it is obligatory to read His words ﴿will be overcome﴾ (sa-yughlabun) with a vowelled "ya'" (i.e., with a damma), so that the meaning would be: "and they, after their being overcome by the Persians, will be overcome by the Muslims," so that the sense of the speech is sound. Otherwise, if the "ya'" were opened, the speech would not have much meaning, because a report about what has already happened would turn into a report about what will happen, and that would corrupt one of the two reports by the other.

* *

As for His words ﴿within a few years﴾:
We have already mentioned the disagreement among the interpreters regarding the meaning of "bid'" (a few) earlier, and we have presented the sound of their views, sufficient to not repeat it in this place.
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Khallad ibn Aslam al-Saffar related to us, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: "I asked him, 'What is al-bid'?' He said: 'The People of the Book claim that it is nine or seven.'"

As for His words ﴿to God belongs the command, before and after﴾: Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His words ﴿to God belongs the command, before﴾: the dominion of Persia over the Romans; ﴿and after﴾: the dominion of the Romans over Persia.

As for His words ﴿and on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God; He gives victory to whom He wills﴾: we have already mentioned the report concerning its interpretation earlier and explained its meaning.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿God's promise—God does not fail His promise, but most people do not know﴾ (6)

Exalted is He, His remembrance: God's promise, the promise that the Romans will overcome Persia after Persia's victory over them. The phrase ﴿God's promise﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun from His words ﴿and they, after their defeat, will overcome﴾, because it is a promise from God to them that they will overcome, as if He had said: God promised the believers that promise as a promise. ﴿God does not fail His promise﴾: Exalted is He, His remembrance: God fulfills His promise to the believers that the Romans will overcome Persia; He does not fail them in that promise, because there is no failing in His promises. ﴿But most people do not know﴾: that is, but most of the Quraysh, who deny that God will fulfill His promise to the believers that the Romans will overcome Persia, do not know that this is so, and that it is not possible for there to be a failure in God's promise.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾ (7)

Exalted is He, His remembrance: These deniers know the outward appearance of the worldly life—the truth of God's report that the Romans will overcome Persia—namely the management of their livelihoods within it and what suits them, while concerning the affair of their Hereafter, and what salvation from God's punishment there lies in it, they are heedless and do not reflect upon it.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Abu Tumayla Yahya ibn Wadih al-Ansari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, saying: Yazid al-Nahwi related to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he means their livelihoods—when they reap and when they plant.
• Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to me, saying: Amr ibn Uthman ibn Umar related to us, from Asim ibn Ali, who said: Abu Tumayla related to us, who said: Ibn Waqid related to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: when they sow, when they plant.
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, saying: Shariqi related to me, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: it is the lamp-maker or the like.
• Abu Huraira Muhammad ibn Firas al-Dab'i related to us, saying: Abu Qutayba related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the lamp-makers."
• Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the leather-workers and the lamp-makers."
• Bishr ibn Adam related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods and what suits them."
• Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
• Bishr ibn Adam related to me, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, and from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods."
• Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he means the disbelievers, who know the prosperity of the world, but in matters of religion they are ignorant.
• Ibn WakI' related to me, saying: my father related to me, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods and what suits them."
• Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: from its trades, its dealings and its pursuits; ﴿and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾.
• Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: "They know when to sow and when to harvest."
• He said: Hafs ibn Rashid al-Hilali related to us, from Shu'ba, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the lamp-maker and the like."
• Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya, who said: "[they spend it] on their livelihood."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾: [[As in the manuscripts; the explanation is not mentioned. It may have slipped from the copyist's pen, or perhaps it is the word "nahwahu" or "mithluhu," which he often omits.]]

Others said something else concerning this:
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "The devils steal the hearing, and they hear the word that has been sent down and which should be in the earth. They are pelted with shooting stars, and none escapes without being burned, or without a spark from it striking him. He falls and never returns. The one who heard it conveys it to his allies among mankind, and they add a thousand lies to it. Then people are seen saying, 'Such-and-such will happen,' and the true part of it comes about just as they say—the part they heard from the heavens—while the lies they immersed themselves in follow it."

The Exposition of the Words of God, Most High: "Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years. To God belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory. He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful." (Q 30:1–5)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained in what came before the meaning of His words "Alif, Lam, Mim" and mentioned what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said about it, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

As for His words: "The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land."

The reciters differed over its recitation. The majority of the reciters of the cities recited "ghulibat al-Rum" (غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ) with a dammah on the ghayn, meaning that Persia (Faris) defeated the Romans.

It was also narrated from Ibn 'Umar and Abu Sa'id concerning this:

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from al-Hasan al-Jufari, from Sulayt, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Alif Lam Mim, ghalabat al-Rum" (غَلَبَتِ الرُّومُ). It was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, over what did they gain the upper hand?" He said: "Over the countryside of al-Sham."

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, which it is not permissible to depart from, is "Alif Lam Mim, ghulibat al-Rum" with a dammah on the ghayn, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters is upon it. Since this is so, the meaning of the speech is: Persia overcame the Romans "in the nearest land" from the land of al-Sham to the land of Persia. "And they, after their defeat," means: and the Romans, after the Persians' victory over them, "will overcome" Persia "within a few years." "To God belongs the command before" their defeat by Persia "and after" their defeat of it. He decrees among His creatures what He wills, judges what He desires, and makes victorious whom He wishes among them over whom He loves to make victorious. "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory": that is, on the day the Romans overcome Persia, the believers in God and His Messenger will rejoice in God's granting them victory over the polytheists, and in the Romans' victory over Persia. "He grants victory" — God, may His remembrance be exalted — "to whom He wills" of His creatures, over whom He wills; and this is the victory of the believers over the polytheists at Badr. "And He is the Mighty": that is, God is severe in His retribution against His enemies, none can prevent Him from that, and no barrier can come between Him and it. "The Merciful" to those of His creatures who repent and return to obedience to Him, so that He does not punish them.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said in this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id, or Sa'id al-Tha'labi, who is called Abu Sa'd, from the people of Tarsus, narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Muslims loved that the Romans, the People of the Book, would overcome, and the polytheists loved that the Persians would overcome, because they were idol-worshippers. He said: They mentioned that to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, they will be defeated." He said: Abu Bakr mentioned that to the polytheists, and they said: "Shall we make a term between us and you? If they are victorious, you will have such and such, and if we are victorious, we will have such and such." He said: So they set between themselves and him a term of five years. He said: It passed, and they were not overcome. He said: Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to him: "Why did you not make it less than ten?" Sa'id said: The bid' is less than ten. He said: So the Romans prevailed, and then were defeated. He said: That is His saying: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years." He said: The bid': what is less than ten. "To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory." Sufyan said: It reached me that they prevailed on the day of Badr.

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Harun al-Bardi narrated to us, saying: Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land..." was revealed, Abu Bakr made a wager with the Quraysh, then came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "I have made a wager with them." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Why did you not take precaution? For the bid' is what is between three and nine." Al-Jumahi said: al-munahaba is al-muraahana (the wager), and that was before the prohibition of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated..." up to His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory." He said: It has passed; it occurred concerning the people of Persia and the Romans, and Persia had defeated them, then the Romans overcame them after that. The Prophet of God ﷺ met the polytheists of the Arabs on the day the Romans and Persians met, so God gave victory to the Prophet ﷺ and those with him among the Muslims over the polytheists of the Arabs, and gave victory to the People of the Book over the polytheists of the non-Arabs, so the believers rejoiced at God's victory granted to them, and the victory of the People of the Book over the non-Arabs. 'Ata' said: I asked Abu Sa'id al-Khudri about that, and he said: "We met with Muhammad the Messenger of God ﷺ and the polytheists of the Arabs, and the Romans and Persians met, so God gave us victory over the polytheists of the Arabs, and God gave victory to the People of the Book over the Magians. We rejoiced at God's victory granted to us over the polytheists, and we rejoiced at God's victory granted to the People of the Book over the Magians." That is His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory."

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome," — Persia had defeated them, then the Romans overcame.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: 'Abd Allah said: Five have already passed: the smoke, the grip, the assault, the moon, and the Romans.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated" has already passed.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated..." up to His saying: "But most of the people do not know." He said: It mentions the defeat of Persia over them, and the Romans' reversal over Persia, and the believers rejoiced at the victory of the Romans, the People of the Book, over Persia, the people of idols.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ikrima, that the Romans and Persians fought in the nearest land. They said: The nearest land at that time was Adhri'at, where they met, and the Romans were routed. This news reached the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, who were in Makkah, and it grieved them. The Prophet ﷺ disliked that the Ummi Magians should prevail over the People of the Book, the Romans. The unbelievers in Makkah rejoiced and gloated, and they met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, while we are Ummis. Our brothers, the people of Persia, have prevailed over your brothers, the People of the Book, and if you fight us, we will surely prevail over you." So God revealed: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years. To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory..." the verses. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq went out to the unbelievers and said: "Have you rejoiced at the victory of your brothers over our brothers? Do not rejoice, and may God not gladden your eyes. By God, the Romans will surely overcome Persia; our Prophet ﷺ informed us of that." Ubayy ibn Khalaf stood up before him and said: "You lie, O Abu Fudayl." Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said to him: "You are the liar, O enemy of God." He said: "I will make a wager with you: ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans overcome Persia, I will pay, and if Persia overcomes the Romans, you will pay, within three years." Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "That is not how I mentioned it; the bid' is what is between three and nine. Increase the stake and extend the term for him." Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy, and said: "Perhaps you have regretted it?" He said: "No." He said: "I will increase the stake for you and extend the term for you; make it a hundred she-camels for a hundred she-camels, for nine years." He said: "I have done so."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrima, who said: In Persia there was a woman who bore only kings and heroes. Khosrow summoned her and said: "I wish to send an army against the Romans and appoint over them a man from your sons, so advise me which of them I should appoint." She said: "This is so-and-so, and he is craftier than a fox and more wary than a sparrow-hawk; and this is Farkhan, and he is more piercing than a spear; and this is Shahrbaraz, and he is more forbearing than such-and-such. Appoint whichever you wish." He said: "I have appointed the forbearing one," and he appointed Shahrbaraz. He marched against the Romans with the people of Persia, prevailed over them, killed them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees. Abu Bakr said: I related this hadith to 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and he said: "Have you not seen the lands of al-Sham?" I said: "No." He said: "Had you seen them, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down." Then I came to al-Sham after that and saw it.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: Yahya ibn Ya'mar related to me that Caesar sent a man called Qitmah with an army of Romans, and Khosrow sent Shahrbaraz. They met at Adhri'at and Busra, which are the nearest of al-Sham to you. Persia met the Romans and defeated them, and the unbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced at that, and the Muslims disliked it, so God revealed: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land..." the verses. Then he mentioned a similar account to the hadith of 'Ikrima, and added: Shahrbaraz continued to trample them and destroy their cities until he reached the channel (al-Khalij). Then Khosrow died, and news of his death reached them, so Shahrbaraz and his companions fled, and the Romans came upon them then, pursuing them and killing them. He said: 'Ikrima also said in his narration: When Persia prevailed over the Romans, Farkhan sat drinking, and said to his companions: "I saw myself as if I were sitting on the throne of Khosrow." This reached Khosrow, who wrote to Shahrbaraz: "When my letter reaches you, send me the head of Farkhan." He wrote back: "O King, you will not find anyone like Farkhan; he has strength and striking power against the enemy, so do not do it." He wrote again: "Among the men of Persia there are substitutes for him; hasten his head to me." He replied again, and Khosrow grew angry and did not answer him. He sent a courier to the people of Persia: "I have removed Shahrbaraz from you and appointed Farkhan over you." Then he gave the courier a small document: "When Farkhan is made king and his brother submits to him, give him this." When Shahrbaraz read the letter, he said: "I hear and obey," and he got down from his throne, and Farkhan sat, and he handed him the document. Farkhan said: "Bring Shahrbaraz to me," and he was brought forward to have his neck struck. He said: "Do not hasten until I write my will." He said: "Yes." So he called for the box, and gave him three documents, and said: "I have argued with Khosrow about you in all of this, and you wanted to kill me with one letter." So the king returned him, and Shahrbaraz wrote to Caesar, king of the Romans: "I have a request that a courier cannot carry and letters cannot convey, so meet me, and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, and I will meet you with fifty Persians." Caesar came with five hundred thousand Romans and set spies before him along the road, fearing that he had plotted against him, until his spies told him that there were with him only fifty men. Then they spread out for the two of them, and they met in a brocade pavilion set up for them, each with a knife. They called for an interpreter between them, and Shahrbaraz said: "It was I and my brother who destroyed your cities, by our cunning and courage, and Khosrow envied us, so he wanted me to kill my brother, and I refused; then he ordered my brother to kill me. So we have both renounced him, and we will fight him with you." He said: "You have done right." Then one of them signaled to his companion that a secret is between two, and when it passes beyond two it spreads. He said: "Indeed." So they both killed the interpreter with their knives. God destroyed Khosrow, and the news reached the Messenger of God ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyya, and he rejoiced, and those with him.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated," he said: Persia defeated them at the nearest part of al-Sham. "But they, after their defeat, will overcome..." the verse. He said: When God revealed these verses, the Muslims affirmed their Lord and knew that the Romans would prevail over Persia, so they and the polytheists wagered five she-camels each, with a term of five years between them. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, took charge of the Muslims' wager, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf took charge of the polytheists' wager, and that was before gambling was forbidden. The term came, and the Romans had not prevailed over Persia, and the polytheists demanded their wager. The Companions of the Prophet mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "You were not worthy to set the term at less than ten, for the bid' is what is between three and ten. Increase the stake for them and extend the term." They did so, and God made the Romans prevail over Persia at the end of the bid' years from their first wager, and that was on his return from al-Hudaybiyya. The Muslims rejoiced at their treaty that had been made, and at the victory of the People of the Book over the Magians, and that was one of the things by which God strengthened Islam, and it is His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory..." the verse.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans..." up to His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice": He said: The Prophet ﷺ had informed the people in Makkah that the Romans would be victorious. He said: So the Qur'an was revealed with that. He said: The Muslims loved the victory of the Romans over Persia, because they were People of the Book.

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Mahhari narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, from 'Abd Allah, who said: Persia was dominant over the Romans, and the polytheists loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book, and closer to their religion. When "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated" to "within a few years" was revealed, they said: "O Abu Bakr, your companion says that the Romans will prevail over Persia within a few years." He said: "He has spoken the truth." They said: "Would you like us to wager with you?" They pledged to him four she-camels for seven years. The seven years passed and nothing happened, so the polytheists rejoiced at that, and it grieved the Muslims. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "What is 'a few years' to you?" They said: "Less than ten." He said: "Go, increase the stake for them and add two years." He said: The two years had not passed before the riders came with news of the Romans' victory over Persia, and the Muslims rejoiced at that. Then God revealed: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated..." up to His saying: "God's promise; God does not fail His promise."

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash and Mutar, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Romans have passed on.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated in the nearest land": He said: The nearest land is al-Sham. "But they, after their defeat, will overcome": He said: Persia had defeated the Romans, then the Romans were given victory over Persia. It is mentioned that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The Romans will surely overcome Persia." The polytheists said: "This is something Muhammad fabricates." Abu Bakr said: "Will you make a wager with me?" — and al-munahaba is al-mujaʿala (the wager) — they said: "Yes." So Abu Bakr made a wager with them and set the years at four or five. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The bid' is between three and nine. Go back to the people and increase the wager." So he returned to them, and they wagered again, and he increased it. He said: So the Romans overcame Persia, and that is God's saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory, He grants victory to whom He wills," on the day the Romans were given victory over Persia.

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated": He said: They were defeated and they defeated; as for those who read it "ghalabat al-Rum" with a fatha on the ghayn, they said: this verse was revealed as a report from God to His Prophet ﷺ about the Romans' victory.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 1–7 (part 2 of 2):

Mention of those who said that:
• Nasr ibn Ali related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from Sulayman—that is, al-A'mash—from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day came when the Romans overcame the Persians, this pleased the believers, and so ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ was revealed about their victory over the Persians."
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Abu Awana related to us, from Sulayman, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the Romans were defeated by the Persians, and the Muslims rejoiced at that. So God revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated...﴾ to the end of the verse."
• Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to us, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the Romans were overcome by the Persians, and this pleased the believers, because they were People of the Book. So God revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land﴾." He said: "They had been defeated before that, and then he recited until he reached ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the nearest land﴾:
I have already mentioned the view of some of them earlier, and I will mention the view of those whose view has not been mentioned.
• Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿in the nearest land﴾: he said, "It means: at the edge of Syria." The meaning of "adna" (nearest) is "aqrab" (closer), and it is the comparative form from "dunuww" and "qurb" (nearness). Its meaning is: "in the land nearest to Persia," and the mention of Persia was omitted because of what is indicated by the phrase ﴿in the nearest land﴾ concerning it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and they, after their defeat﴾:
It means: the Romans, after the Persians' defeat of them, will overcome the Persians.

* *

As for His words ﴿after their defeat﴾:
It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "ghalabtuhu ghalaba" (I overcame him with an overcoming), so the "ha'" (the feminine ending) was dropped from "ghalaba." It has also been said: "min ba'di ghalabihim" (after their defeat), and he did not say "min ba'di ghalabatihim" (after their defeat, with the feminine ending) because of the annexation (idafa), just as it was dropped in His words ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾ because of the annexation; the original phrase is "wa iqamat al-salah" (and the establishment of the prayer).
As for His words ﴿will overcome﴾ (sa-yaghlibun), all the readers agree on opening the "ya'" in it. According to the reading of one who reads ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been overcome﴾ with an opened "ghayn," it is obligatory to read His words ﴿will be overcome﴾ (sa-yughlabun) with a vowelled "ya'" (i.e., with a damma), so that the meaning would be: "and they, after their being overcome by the Persians, will be overcome by the Muslims," so that the sense of the speech is sound. Otherwise, if the "ya'" were opened, the speech would not have much meaning, because a report about what has already happened would turn into a report about what will happen, and that would corrupt one of the two reports by the other.

* *

As for His words ﴿within a few years﴾:
We have already mentioned the disagreement among the interpreters regarding the meaning of "bid'" (a few) earlier, and we have presented the sound of their views, sufficient to not repeat it in this place.
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Khallad ibn Aslam al-Saffar related to us, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: "I asked him, 'What is al-bid'?' He said: 'The People of the Book claim that it is nine or seven.'"

As for His words ﴿to God belongs the command, before and after﴾: Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His words ﴿to God belongs the command, before﴾: the dominion of Persia over the Romans; ﴿and after﴾: the dominion of the Romans over Persia.

As for His words ﴿and on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God; He gives victory to whom He wills﴾: we have already mentioned the report concerning its interpretation earlier and explained its meaning.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿God's promise—God does not fail His promise, but most people do not know﴾ (6)

Exalted is He, His remembrance: God's promise, the promise that the Romans will overcome Persia after Persia's victory over them. The phrase ﴿God's promise﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun from His words ﴿and they, after their defeat, will overcome﴾, because it is a promise from God to them that they will overcome, as if He had said: God promised the believers that promise as a promise. ﴿God does not fail His promise﴾: Exalted is He, His remembrance: God fulfills His promise to the believers that the Romans will overcome Persia; He does not fail them in that promise, because there is no failing in His promises. ﴿But most people do not know﴾: that is, but most of the Quraysh, who deny that God will fulfill His promise to the believers that the Romans will overcome Persia, do not know that this is so, and that it is not possible for there to be a failure in God's promise.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾ (7)

Exalted is He, His remembrance: These deniers know the outward appearance of the worldly life—the truth of God's report that the Romans will overcome Persia—namely the management of their livelihoods within it and what suits them, while concerning the affair of their Hereafter, and what salvation from God's punishment there lies in it, they are heedless and do not reflect upon it.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Abu Tumayla Yahya ibn Wadih al-Ansari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, saying: Yazid al-Nahwi related to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he means their livelihoods—when they reap and when they plant.
• Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to me, saying: Amr ibn Uthman ibn Umar related to us, from Asim ibn Ali, who said: Abu Tumayla related to us, who said: Ibn Waqid related to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: when they sow, when they plant.
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, saying: Shariqi related to me, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: it is the lamp-maker or the like.
• Abu Huraira Muhammad ibn Firas al-Dab'i related to us, saying: Abu Qutayba related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the lamp-makers."
• Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the leather-workers and the lamp-makers."
• Bishr ibn Adam related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods and what suits them."
• Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
• Bishr ibn Adam related to me, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, and from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods."
• Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he means the disbelievers, who know the prosperity of the world, but in matters of religion they are ignorant.
• Ibn WakI' related to me, saying: my father related to me, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods and what suits them."
• Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: from its trades, its dealings and its pursuits; ﴿and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾.
• Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: "They know when to sow and when to harvest."
• He said: Hafs ibn Rashid al-Hilali related to us, from Shu'ba, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the lamp-maker and the like."
• Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya, who said: "[they spend it] on their livelihood."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾: [[As in the manuscripts; the explanation is not mentioned. It may have slipped from the copyist's pen, or perhaps it is the word "nahwahu" or "mithluhu," which he often omits.]]

Others said something else concerning this:
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "The devils steal the hearing, and they hear the word that has been sent down and which should be in the earth. They are pelted with shooting stars, and none escapes without being burned, or without a spark from it striking him. He falls and never returns. The one who heard it conveys it to his allies among mankind, and they add a thousand lies to it. Then people are seen saying, 'Such-and-such will happen,' and the true part of it comes about just as they say—the part they heard from the heavens—while the lies they immersed themselves in follow it."

The Exposition of the Words of God, Most High: "Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years. To God belongs the command, before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory. He grants victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful." (Q 30:1–5)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained in what came before the meaning of His words "Alif, Lam, Mim" and mentioned what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said about it, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

* *

As for His words: "The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land."

The reciters differed over its recitation. The majority of the reciters of the cities recited "ghulibat al-Rum" (غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ) with a dammah on the ghayn, meaning that Persia (Faris) defeated the Romans.

It was also narrated from Ibn 'Umar and Abu Sa'id concerning this:

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from al-Hasan al-Jufari, from Sulayt, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Alif Lam Mim, ghalabat al-Rum" (غَلَبَتِ الرُّومُ). It was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, over what did they gain the upper hand?" He said: "Over the countryside of al-Sham."

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, which it is not permissible to depart from, is "Alif Lam Mim, ghulibat al-Rum" with a dammah on the ghayn, because the consensus of the authoritative reciters is upon it. Since this is so, the meaning of the speech is: Persia overcame the Romans "in the nearest land" from the land of al-Sham to the land of Persia. "And they, after their defeat," means: and the Romans, after the Persians' victory over them, "will overcome" Persia "within a few years." "To God belongs the command before" their defeat by Persia "and after" their defeat of it. He decrees among His creatures what He wills, judges what He desires, and makes victorious whom He wishes among them over whom He loves to make victorious. "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory": that is, on the day the Romans overcome Persia, the believers in God and His Messenger will rejoice in God's granting them victory over the polytheists, and in the Romans' victory over Persia. "He grants victory" — God, may His remembrance be exalted — "to whom He wills" of His creatures, over whom He wills; and this is the victory of the believers over the polytheists at Badr. "And He is the Mighty": that is, God is severe in His retribution against His enemies, none can prevent Him from that, and no barrier can come between Him and it. "The Merciful" to those of His creatures who repent and return to obedience to Him, so that He does not punish them.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said in this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id, or Sa'id al-Tha'labi, who is called Abu Sa'd, from the people of Tarsus, narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Muslims loved that the Romans, the People of the Book, would overcome, and the polytheists loved that the Persians would overcome, because they were idol-worshippers. He said: They mentioned that to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, they will be defeated." He said: Abu Bakr mentioned that to the polytheists, and they said: "Shall we make a term between us and you? If they are victorious, you will have such and such, and if we are victorious, we will have such and such." He said: So they set between themselves and him a term of five years. He said: It passed, and they were not overcome. He said: Abu Bakr mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to him: "Why did you not make it less than ten?" Sa'id said: The bid' is less than ten. He said: So the Romans prevailed, and then were defeated. He said: That is His saying: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years." He said: The bid': what is less than ten. "To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory." Sufyan said: It reached me that they prevailed on the day of Badr.

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Harun al-Bardi narrated to us, saying: Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land..." was revealed, Abu Bakr made a wager with the Quraysh, then came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "I have made a wager with them." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Why did you not take precaution? For the bid' is what is between three and nine." Al-Jumahi said: al-munahaba is al-muraahana (the wager), and that was before the prohibition of it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated..." up to His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory." He said: It has passed; it occurred concerning the people of Persia and the Romans, and Persia had defeated them, then the Romans overcame them after that. The Prophet of God ﷺ met the polytheists of the Arabs on the day the Romans and Persians met, so God gave victory to the Prophet ﷺ and those with him among the Muslims over the polytheists of the Arabs, and gave victory to the People of the Book over the polytheists of the non-Arabs, so the believers rejoiced at God's victory granted to them, and the victory of the People of the Book over the non-Arabs. 'Ata' said: I asked Abu Sa'id al-Khudri about that, and he said: "We met with Muhammad the Messenger of God ﷺ and the polytheists of the Arabs, and the Romans and Persians met, so God gave us victory over the polytheists of the Arabs, and God gave victory to the People of the Book over the Magians. We rejoiced at God's victory granted to us over the polytheists, and we rejoiced at God's victory granted to the People of the Book over the Magians." That is His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory."

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome," — Persia had defeated them, then the Romans overcame.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, who said: 'Abd Allah said: Five have already passed: the smoke, the grip, the assault, the moon, and the Romans.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated" has already passed.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated..." up to His saying: "But most of the people do not know." He said: It mentions the defeat of Persia over them, and the Romans' reversal over Persia, and the believers rejoiced at the victory of the Romans, the People of the Book, over Persia, the people of idols.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ikrima, that the Romans and Persians fought in the nearest land. They said: The nearest land at that time was Adhri'at, where they met, and the Romans were routed. This news reached the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, who were in Makkah, and it grieved them. The Prophet ﷺ disliked that the Ummi Magians should prevail over the People of the Book, the Romans. The unbelievers in Makkah rejoiced and gloated, and they met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, while we are Ummis. Our brothers, the people of Persia, have prevailed over your brothers, the People of the Book, and if you fight us, we will surely prevail over you." So God revealed: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years. To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory..." the verses. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq went out to the unbelievers and said: "Have you rejoiced at the victory of your brothers over our brothers? Do not rejoice, and may God not gladden your eyes. By God, the Romans will surely overcome Persia; our Prophet ﷺ informed us of that." Ubayy ibn Khalaf stood up before him and said: "You lie, O Abu Fudayl." Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said to him: "You are the liar, O enemy of God." He said: "I will make a wager with you: ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans overcome Persia, I will pay, and if Persia overcomes the Romans, you will pay, within three years." Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "That is not how I mentioned it; the bid' is what is between three and nine. Increase the stake and extend the term for him." Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy, and said: "Perhaps you have regretted it?" He said: "No." He said: "I will increase the stake for you and extend the term for you; make it a hundred she-camels for a hundred she-camels, for nine years." He said: "I have done so."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from 'Ikrima, who said: In Persia there was a woman who bore only kings and heroes. Khosrow summoned her and said: "I wish to send an army against the Romans and appoint over them a man from your sons, so advise me which of them I should appoint." She said: "This is so-and-so, and he is craftier than a fox and more wary than a sparrow-hawk; and this is Farkhan, and he is more piercing than a spear; and this is Shahrbaraz, and he is more forbearing than such-and-such. Appoint whichever you wish." He said: "I have appointed the forbearing one," and he appointed Shahrbaraz. He marched against the Romans with the people of Persia, prevailed over them, killed them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees. Abu Bakr said: I related this hadith to 'Ata' al-Khurasani, and he said: "Have you not seen the lands of al-Sham?" I said: "No." He said: "Had you seen them, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down." Then I came to al-Sham after that and saw it.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: Yahya ibn Ya'mar related to me that Caesar sent a man called Qitmah with an army of Romans, and Khosrow sent Shahrbaraz. They met at Adhri'at and Busra, which are the nearest of al-Sham to you. Persia met the Romans and defeated them, and the unbelievers of Quraysh rejoiced at that, and the Muslims disliked it, so God revealed: "Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land..." the verses. Then he mentioned a similar account to the hadith of 'Ikrima, and added: Shahrbaraz continued to trample them and destroy their cities until he reached the channel (al-Khalij). Then Khosrow died, and news of his death reached them, so Shahrbaraz and his companions fled, and the Romans came upon them then, pursuing them and killing them. He said: 'Ikrima also said in his narration: When Persia prevailed over the Romans, Farkhan sat drinking, and said to his companions: "I saw myself as if I were sitting on the throne of Khosrow." This reached Khosrow, who wrote to Shahrbaraz: "When my letter reaches you, send me the head of Farkhan." He wrote back: "O King, you will not find anyone like Farkhan; he has strength and striking power against the enemy, so do not do it." He wrote again: "Among the men of Persia there are substitutes for him; hasten his head to me." He replied again, and Khosrow grew angry and did not answer him. He sent a courier to the people of Persia: "I have removed Shahrbaraz from you and appointed Farkhan over you." Then he gave the courier a small document: "When Farkhan is made king and his brother submits to him, give him this." When Shahrbaraz read the letter, he said: "I hear and obey," and he got down from his throne, and Farkhan sat, and he handed him the document. Farkhan said: "Bring Shahrbaraz to me," and he was brought forward to have his neck struck. He said: "Do not hasten until I write my will." He said: "Yes." So he called for the box, and gave him three documents, and said: "I have argued with Khosrow about you in all of this, and you wanted to kill me with one letter." So the king returned him, and Shahrbaraz wrote to Caesar, king of the Romans: "I have a request that a courier cannot carry and letters cannot convey, so meet me, and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, and I will meet you with fifty Persians." Caesar came with five hundred thousand Romans and set spies before him along the road, fearing that he had plotted against him, until his spies told him that there were with him only fifty men. Then they spread out for the two of them, and they met in a brocade pavilion set up for them, each with a knife. They called for an interpreter between them, and Shahrbaraz said: "It was I and my brother who destroyed your cities, by our cunning and courage, and Khosrow envied us, so he wanted me to kill my brother, and I refused; then he ordered my brother to kill me. So we have both renounced him, and we will fight him with you." He said: "You have done right." Then one of them signaled to his companion that a secret is between two, and when it passes beyond two it spreads. He said: "Indeed." So they both killed the interpreter with their knives. God destroyed Khosrow, and the news reached the Messenger of God ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyya, and he rejoiced, and those with him.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated," he said: Persia defeated them at the nearest part of al-Sham. "But they, after their defeat, will overcome..." the verse. He said: When God revealed these verses, the Muslims affirmed their Lord and knew that the Romans would prevail over Persia, so they and the polytheists wagered five she-camels each, with a term of five years between them. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, took charge of the Muslims' wager, and Ubayy ibn Khalaf took charge of the polytheists' wager, and that was before gambling was forbidden. The term came, and the Romans had not prevailed over Persia, and the polytheists demanded their wager. The Companions of the Prophet mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "You were not worthy to set the term at less than ten, for the bid' is what is between three and ten. Increase the stake for them and extend the term." They did so, and God made the Romans prevail over Persia at the end of the bid' years from their first wager, and that was on his return from al-Hudaybiyya. The Muslims rejoiced at their treaty that had been made, and at the victory of the People of the Book over the Magians, and that was one of the things by which God strengthened Islam, and it is His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory..." the verse.

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans..." up to His saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice": He said: The Prophet ﷺ had informed the people in Makkah that the Romans would be victorious. He said: So the Qur'an was revealed with that. He said: The Muslims loved the victory of the Romans over Persia, because they were People of the Book.

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Mahhari narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amir, from 'Abd Allah, who said: Persia was dominant over the Romans, and the polytheists loved that Persia would prevail over the Romans, and the Muslims loved that the Romans would prevail over Persia, because they were People of the Book, and closer to their religion. When "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated" to "within a few years" was revealed, they said: "O Abu Bakr, your companion says that the Romans will prevail over Persia within a few years." He said: "He has spoken the truth." They said: "Would you like us to wager with you?" They pledged to him four she-camels for seven years. The seven years passed and nothing happened, so the polytheists rejoiced at that, and it grieved the Muslims. They mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "What is 'a few years' to you?" They said: "Less than ten." He said: "Go, increase the stake for them and add two years." He said: The two years had not passed before the riders came with news of the Romans' victory over Persia, and the Muslims rejoiced at that. Then God revealed: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated..." up to His saying: "God's promise; God does not fail His promise."

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash and Mutar, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Romans have passed on.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated in the nearest land": He said: The nearest land is al-Sham. "But they, after their defeat, will overcome": He said: Persia had defeated the Romans, then the Romans were given victory over Persia. It is mentioned that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The Romans will surely overcome Persia." The polytheists said: "This is something Muhammad fabricates." Abu Bakr said: "Will you make a wager with me?" — and al-munahaba is al-mujaʿala (the wager) — they said: "Yes." So Abu Bakr made a wager with them and set the years at four or five. Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The bid' is between three and nine. Go back to the people and increase the wager." So he returned to them, and they wagered again, and he increased it. He said: So the Romans overcame Persia, and that is God's saying: "And on that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory, He grants victory to whom He wills," on the day the Romans were given victory over Persia.

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Alif Lam Mim, the Romans have been defeated": He said: They were defeated and they defeated; as for those who read it "ghalabat al-Rum" with a fatha on the ghayn, they said: this verse was revealed as a report from God to His Prophet ﷺ about the Romans' victory.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 1–7 (part 2 of 2):

Mention of those who said that:
• Nasr ibn Ali related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from Sulayman—that is, al-A'mash—from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day came when the Romans overcame the Persians, this pleased the believers, and so ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ was revealed about their victory over the Persians."
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Abu Awana related to us, from Sulayman, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the Romans were defeated by the Persians, and the Muslims rejoiced at that. So God revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated...﴾ to the end of the verse."
• Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to us, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the Romans were overcome by the Persians, and this pleased the believers, because they were People of the Book. So God revealed ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land﴾." He said: "They had been defeated before that, and then he recited until he reached ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God﴾."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the nearest land﴾:
I have already mentioned the view of some of them earlier, and I will mention the view of those whose view has not been mentioned.
• Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿in the nearest land﴾: he said, "It means: at the edge of Syria." The meaning of "adna" (nearest) is "aqrab" (closer), and it is the comparative form from "dunuww" and "qurb" (nearness). Its meaning is: "in the land nearest to Persia," and the mention of Persia was omitted because of what is indicated by the phrase ﴿in the nearest land﴾ concerning it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and they, after their defeat﴾:
It means: the Romans, after the Persians' defeat of them, will overcome the Persians.

* *

As for His words ﴿after their defeat﴾:
It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "ghalabtuhu ghalaba" (I overcame him with an overcoming), so the "ha'" (the feminine ending) was dropped from "ghalaba." It has also been said: "min ba'di ghalabihim" (after their defeat), and he did not say "min ba'di ghalabatihim" (after their defeat, with the feminine ending) because of the annexation (idafa), just as it was dropped in His words ﴿and the establishment of prayer﴾ because of the annexation; the original phrase is "wa iqamat al-salah" (and the establishment of the prayer).
As for His words ﴿will overcome﴾ (sa-yaghlibun), all the readers agree on opening the "ya'" in it. According to the reading of one who reads ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been overcome﴾ with an opened "ghayn," it is obligatory to read His words ﴿will be overcome﴾ (sa-yughlabun) with a vowelled "ya'" (i.e., with a damma), so that the meaning would be: "and they, after their being overcome by the Persians, will be overcome by the Muslims," so that the sense of the speech is sound. Otherwise, if the "ya'" were opened, the speech would not have much meaning, because a report about what has already happened would turn into a report about what will happen, and that would corrupt one of the two reports by the other.

* *

As for His words ﴿within a few years﴾:
We have already mentioned the disagreement among the interpreters regarding the meaning of "bid'" (a few) earlier, and we have presented the sound of their views, sufficient to not repeat it in this place.
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Khallad ibn Aslam al-Saffar related to us, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: "I asked him, 'What is al-bid'?' He said: 'The People of the Book claim that it is nine or seven.'"

As for His words ﴿to God belongs the command, before and after﴾: Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His words ﴿to God belongs the command, before﴾: the dominion of Persia over the Romans; ﴿and after﴾: the dominion of the Romans over Persia.

As for His words ﴿and on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God; He gives victory to whom He wills﴾: we have already mentioned the report concerning its interpretation earlier and explained its meaning.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿God's promise—God does not fail His promise, but most people do not know﴾ (6)

Exalted is He, His remembrance: God's promise, the promise that the Romans will overcome Persia after Persia's victory over them. The phrase ﴿God's promise﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun from His words ﴿and they, after their defeat, will overcome﴾, because it is a promise from God to them that they will overcome, as if He had said: God promised the believers that promise as a promise. ﴿God does not fail His promise﴾: Exalted is He, His remembrance: God fulfills His promise to the believers that the Romans will overcome Persia; He does not fail them in that promise, because there is no failing in His promises. ﴿But most people do not know﴾: that is, but most of the Quraysh, who deny that God will fulfill His promise to the believers that the Romans will overcome Persia, do not know that this is so, and that it is not possible for there to be a failure in God's promise.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾ (7)

Exalted is He, His remembrance: These deniers know the outward appearance of the worldly life—the truth of God's report that the Romans will overcome Persia—namely the management of their livelihoods within it and what suits them, while concerning the affair of their Hereafter, and what salvation from God's punishment there lies in it, they are heedless and do not reflect upon it.

The interpreters have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Abu Tumayla Yahya ibn Wadih al-Ansari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, saying: Yazid al-Nahwi related to us, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he means their livelihoods—when they reap and when they plant.
• Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to me, saying: Amr ibn Uthman ibn Umar related to us, from Asim ibn Ali, who said: Abu Tumayla related to us, who said: Ibn Waqid related to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: when they sow, when they plant.
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, saying: Shariqi related to me, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: it is the lamp-maker or the like.
• Abu Huraira Muhammad ibn Firas al-Dab'i related to us, saying: Abu Qutayba related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the lamp-makers."
• Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the leather-workers and the lamp-makers."
• Bishr ibn Adam related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods and what suits them."
• Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
• Bishr ibn Adam related to me, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, and from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods."
• Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he means the disbelievers, who know the prosperity of the world, but in matters of religion they are ignorant.
• Ibn WakI' related to me, saying: my father related to me, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "their livelihoods and what suits them."
• Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: from its trades, its dealings and its pursuits; ﴿and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾.
• Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: "They know when to sow and when to harvest."
• He said: Hafs ibn Rashid al-Hilali related to us, from Shu'ba, from Shariqi, from Ikrima, concerning ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "the lamp-maker and the like."
• Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya, who said: "[they spend it] on their livelihood."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, and they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾: [[As in the manuscripts; the explanation is not mentioned. It may have slipped from the copyist's pen, or perhaps it is the word "nahwahu" or "mithluhu," which he often omits.]]

Others said something else concerning this:
• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, concerning His words ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life﴾: he said: "The devils steal the hearing, and they hear the word that has been sent down and which should be in the earth. They are pelted with shooting stars, and none escapes without being burned, or without a spark from it striking him. He falls and never returns. The one who heard it conveys it to his allies among mankind, and they add a thousand lies to it. Then people are seen saying, 'Such-and-such will happen,' and the true part of it comes about just as they say—the part they heard from the heavens—while the lies they immersed themselves in follow it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 8:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term. Yet many of the people are, in the meeting with their Lord, disbelievers.﴾ (30:8)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these deniers of the Resurrection, O Muhammad, from among your people, not reflected upon God's creation of them, and that He created them when they were nothing, then changed them through states and stages until they became men, so that they might know that the One who did that is able to restore them after their annihilation as a new creation, and then recompense the good-doer among them for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, not wronging any of them, so that He would punish one for another's crime, nor depriving any of them of the reward of his deed, for He is the Just who does not oppress? ﴿What God created of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ is only with justice and the establishment of truth. ﴿And for a specified term﴾: he says, and for a fixed, appointed term; when it reaches that time, He will annihilate all of it, replace the earth with other than the earth and the heavens, and they will come forth before God, the One, the Subduer. Indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are deniers and rejecters, out of ignorance that their return is to God after their annihilation, and heedlessness of the Hereafter.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength, and they stirred up the earth and populated it more than these have populated it. And their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And God would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (30:9)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these deniers of God, heedless of the Hereafter, from among the Quraysh, not traveled in the lands they pass through for trade, so that they might look at the signs of God regarding those who came before them from the denying nations, and how was the end of their affair in denying their messengers? They were stronger than them, ﴿and they stirred up the earth﴾: he says: they excavated the earth, tilled it, and populated it more than these people have populated it, so God destroyed them for their disbelief and their denial of their messengers, and they were unable to ward off, despite the strength of their powers, the punishment of God that descended upon them, and their populating of what they populated of the earth did not benefit them, since ﴿their messengers came to them with the clear proofs﴾ of the signs, and they denied them, so God brought down upon them His might. ﴿And God would not have wronged them﴾ by punishing them for their denial of His messengers and their rejection of His signs, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾ by their disobedience to their Lord.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words, ﴿and they stirred up the earth﴾, the people of interpretation said:

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength, and they stirred up the earth and populated it more than these have populated it.﴾ He said: they possessed the earth and populated it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and they stirred up the earth﴾, he said: they tilled it.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth...﴾ up to His words ﴿and they stirred up the earth and populated it﴾, like His words ﴿and traces in the earth﴾, and His words ﴿and populated it more than these have populated it﴾ ﴿and their messengers came to them with clear evidences﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 9–10:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst [of endings], because they denied the signs of Allah and used to mock them﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Then the final outcome of those among these people who disbelieved, who tilled the earth and cultivated it, and whose messengers came to them with clear proofs from Allah, and who denied their messengers, was that they did evil by their conduct.

﴿al-Su'a (the worst)﴾: it means the state that is worse than their deeds. As for this world, it is ruin and destruction; and as for the Hereafter, it is the Fire, from which they will not come out, nor will they be allowed to make amends.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾: "Those who associated partners [with Allah] — al-su'a: that is, the Fire."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾, he said: "Those who disbelieved, their recompense is the punishment."

Some of the grammarians said: al-su'a in this place is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-buqwa; but others disagreed with him and said it is a noun (ism).

* *

And His saying: ﴿that they denied the signs of Allah﴾

He says: the worst end was theirs, because they denied the signs of Allah in the world, ﴿and they used to mock them﴾. He says: they used to mock the proofs of Allah, namely His prophets and messengers.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 9–10:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst [of endings], because they denied the signs of Allah and used to mock them﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Then the final outcome of those among these people who disbelieved, who tilled the earth and cultivated it, and whose messengers came to them with clear proofs from Allah, and who denied their messengers, was that they did evil by their conduct.

﴿al-Su'a (the worst)﴾: it means the state that is worse than their deeds. As for this world, it is ruin and destruction; and as for the Hereafter, it is the Fire, from which they will not come out, nor will they be allowed to make amends.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾: "Those who associated partners [with Allah] — al-su'a: that is, the Fire."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst﴾, he said: "Those who disbelieved, their recompense is the punishment."

Some of the grammarians said: al-su'a in this place is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-buqwa; but others disagreed with him and said it is a noun (ism).

* *

And His saying: ﴿that they denied the signs of Allah﴾

He says: the worst end was theirs, because they denied the signs of Allah in the world, ﴿and they used to mock them﴾. He says: they used to mock the proofs of Allah, namely His prophets and messengers.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 11–13:

The interpretation of His words, ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned﴾ (11):

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Allah, may He be exalted, originates the creation of all beings, alone in its origination, without any associate or helper. He brings it into existence from nothing, but by His power, mighty and majestic is He.
