Then He repeats creation anew after its annihilation and its nullification, just as He originated it as a sound creation, when it was not a thing at all. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾: He says, then to Him, after their renewal as a new creation, they will be sent back, and they will be gathered for the decisive judgment between them, ﴿that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His words, ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be despairing (yublisu). And they will have no intercessors from their associates, and they will be disbelievers in their associates﴾ (12–13):

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: And on the day the Hour comes, the Hour in which Allah will judge between His creatures, and in which the dead will be raised from their graves, and He will gather them to the place of reckoning. ﴿The criminals will be despairing (yublisu)﴾: meaning, those who associated others with Allah and earned in the world the evil deeds of every kind of wrong will despair, be dejected and regret, as al-'Ajjaj said:

"O companion, do you recognise a worn-out trace (rasman mukarrasan)?
He said: Yes, I recognise it, and he despaired (wa-ablasa)."

[The two verses are in rajaz by al-'Ajjaj (his Diwan, Leipzig edition 1903, p. 31), and in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 247) and Abu 'Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 186b). Abu 'Ubayda, explaining His words "And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be despairing," said: that is, they will regret, be dejected and despair, and he recited "O companion..." the two verses. In Lisan al-'Arab (root k-r-s): a "rasm mukarras" (passive participle) and "mukarris" (active participle) is a trace in which camels have dropped dung and urine, so that some of it is piled upon other parts. And under (b-l-s): ablasa al-rajul means he was cut off, according to Tha'lab; and ablasa: he fell silent; and ablasa min rahmat Allah: he despaired and regretted.]

And the people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿yublisu﴾: He said: it means "yaktali'" (they will be dejected).

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words ﴿The criminals will be despairing﴾: meaning, in the Fire.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of Allah ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be despairing﴾: He said: the mublis is one upon whom evil has descended; when a man is ablasa, then calamity has descended upon him.

* *

As for His words, ﴿And they will have no intercessors from their associates﴾:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 11–13:

The interpretation of His words, ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned﴾ (11):

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Allah, may He be exalted, originates the creation of all beings, alone in its origination, without any associate or helper. He brings it into existence from nothing, but by His power, mighty and majestic is He. Then He repeats creation anew after its annihilation and its nullification, just as He originated it as a sound creation, when it was not a thing at all. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾: He says, then to Him, after their renewal as a new creation, they will be sent back, and they will be gathered for the decisive judgment between them, ﴿that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His words, ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be despairing (yublisu). And they will have no intercessors from their associates, and they will be disbelievers in their associates﴾ (12–13):

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: And on the day the Hour comes, the Hour in which Allah will judge between His creatures, and in which the dead will be raised from their graves, and He will gather them to the place of reckoning. ﴿The criminals will be despairing (yublisu)﴾: meaning, those who associated others with Allah and earned in the world the evil deeds of every kind of wrong will despair, be dejected and regret, as al-'Ajjaj said:

"O companion, do you recognise a worn-out trace (rasman mukarrasan)?
He said: Yes, I recognise it, and he despaired (wa-ablasa)."

[The two verses are in rajaz by al-'Ajjaj (his Diwan, Leipzig edition 1903, p. 31), and in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 247) and Abu 'Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 186b). Abu 'Ubayda, explaining His words "And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will be despairing," said: that is, they will regret, be dejected and despair, and he recited "O companion..." the two verses. In Lisan al-'Arab (root k-r-s): a "rasm mukarras" (passive participle) and "mukarris" (active participle) is a trace in which camels have dropped dung and urine, so that some of it is piled upon other parts. And under (b-l-s): ablasa al-rajul means he was cut off, according to Tha'lab; and ablasa: he fell silent; and ablasa min rahmat Allah: he despaired and regretted.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 14–15:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated﴾ ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾

His, the Exalted's, mention says: "And the Day the Hour comes, when creation will be gathered to God, on that Day," He says, ﴿they will be separated﴾, meaning: the people of faith in God and the people of disbelief in Him will be separated. As for the people of faith, they will be led by the right side to Paradise, and as for the people of disbelief, they will be led by the left side to the Fire. There, God will distinguish the wicked from the good.

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated﴾. He said: "A separation, by God, with no gathering after it." ﴿As for those who believed﴾ in God and His Messenger ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: they acted upon what God commanded them and refrained from what He forbade them, ﴿they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾. He said: they will be among the sweet herbs and dense plants, and among the varieties of flowers in the Gardens, rejoicing and taking pleasure, enjoying listening and a pleasant, agreeable life. God, may His praise be exalted, specifically mentioned the meadow in this context because there was nothing more beautiful in appearance or more fragrant in scent than meadows among the two extremes. And what shows that this is so is the saying of A'sha of Banu Tha'laba:

*How many a meadow of beauty, luxuriant,*
*Green, watered by a pouring, abundant rain,*

*The sun is laughed at by its star, radiant,*
*Wrapped in a dense growth of plants, mature.*

*No day is more fragrant in its scent,*
*Nor more beautiful than it, when the evening approaches.* [[The three verses are by A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 57), and the reading there is: "min riyad al-hazn" (from the meadows of the highlands), which is the elevated land. Abu 'Ubayda cited the first and third verses in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 187), and the reading there is: "min riyad al-hazm," meaning the same as al-hazn, i.e., rough land. Abu 'Ubayda said: "(in a meadow, delighted): its metaphor is 'they rejoice and take pleasure.' Nothing is more beautiful to the Arabs than meadows full of plants, nor more fragrant" — and he cites A'sha's "How many a meadow..." etc. I say: the reading "al-hazn" or "al-hazm" is the best of the readings, and the meadows of highlands are more fragrant than those of lowlands, because the wind blows over them and stirs their scent, and because feet do not trample them, and because the sun strikes them from all sides, so their crops flourish and thrive. Al-Musbil: the rain. Al-Hatl: abundant. Al-Kawkab: the light; al-Sharq: bright and radiant; al-Mu'assar: that around which there is another plant, so it is like a waist-wrap for it. Al-Muktahil: that which has reached maturity and completeness. Al-Nashr: the spreading of scent. Al-Asal: plural of asil, the time of sunset or shortly before it, when the sun turns yellow and draws near to setting.]]

Thus He informed them, the Exalted, that those who believed and did righteous deeds will have a delightful sight, pleasant fragrances, and a pleasant life in what they love, rejoice in, and are envied for. And ﴿al-hibra﴾ among the Arabs means joy and envy-worthy happiness. Al-'Ajjaj said:

*Praise belongs to God, who gave joy*
*To the clients of truth, for indeed the client is grateful.* [[The two verses are by al-'Ajjaj (his Diwan, Leipzig edition 1903, p. 15), from a rajaz poem praising 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar; cited in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda (folio 187b) as a continuation of A'sha's verse before it. In Lisan al-Arab (h-b-r): al-hibr (with fath then sukun), al-habr (with two fathas), al-habra (with fath then sukun), and al-hubur all mean joy. Al-'Ajjaj said: "Fa-al-hamdu li-llah..." — the verse comes from the saying "habarni hadha al-amr habran," meaning it pleased me; the vowel of the letter ba' is moved in both, and its original form is sukun. Ahbarani al-amr: it pleased me; it is also narrated as al-shabr.]]

The commentators differed about the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning is: ﴿they will be in a meadow, honored﴾.

Those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿so they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾. He said: "honored."

Others said: its meaning is: "they will be blessed."

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿yujbarun﴾. He said: "they will be blessed."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿so they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾. He said: "they will be blessed."

Others said: they will take pleasure in listening and singing.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harasi narrated to me, saying: 'Amir ibn Yasaf narrated to me, saying: I asked Yahya ibn Abi Kathir about the saying of God: ﴿so they will be in a meadow, delighted﴾. He said: "al-hibra: pleasure and listening."

* Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Damra ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir regarding His words: ﴿yuhbarun﴾. He said: "listening in Paradise."

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, similarly.

* Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from 'Amir ibn Yasaf, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, similarly.

All of these expressions we have mentioned from those whom we cited return to the meaning we have stated.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 16–18:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into punishment.﴾ (16)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: As for those who denied the Oneness of Allah, denied His messengers, and rejected the resurrection after death and the gathering for the Hereafter, they will be brought into the punishment of Allah. Allah will bring them to it, gathering them there so that they may taste the punishment which they used to deny in the world [[As in the original, with the resumptive pronoun omitted. That is, "which they used to deny it."]].

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning. And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you enter the afternoon.﴾ (17–18)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: So glorify Allah, O people, meaning: pray to Him. ﴿When you enter the evening﴾ refers to the Maghrib prayer, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ refers to the Subh prayer. ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth﴾ means: praise is due to Him from all His creation, to the exclusion of others, ﴿in the heavens﴾ from their inhabitants among the angels, ﴿and the earth﴾ from its people, from all kinds of His creatures therein. ﴿And at night﴾ means: glorify Him also at night, which is the 'Asr prayer. ﴿And when you enter the afternoon﴾ means: and when you enter the time of Zuhr.

The commentators have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn 'Abbas: "Do we find the times of the five prayers in the Book of Allah?" He said: "Yes: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾ is Maghrib, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ is Fajr, ﴿and at night﴾ is 'Asr, ﴿and when you enter the afternoon﴾ is Zuhr." He said: ﴿And after the prayer of 'Isha', three times of privacy for you﴾.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn 'Abbas about the five prayers in the Qur'an, and he said: "Yes," and recited ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾, and said: "It is the Maghrib prayer." ﴿And when you enter the morning﴾, he said: "It is the Subh prayer." ﴿And at night﴾, he said: "It is the 'Asr prayer." ﴿And when you enter the afternoon﴾: "It is the Zuhr prayer." Then he recited: ﴿And after the prayer of 'Isha', three times of privacy for you﴾.

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from al-Hakam ibn Abi 'Iyad, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: These two verses gathered the times of prayer: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾, he said: "Maghrib and 'Isha'." ﴿And when you enter the morning﴾: "Fajr." ﴿And at night﴾: "'Asr." ﴿And when you enter the afternoon﴾: "Zuhr."

Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from al-Hakam, from Abu 'Iyad, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Layth, from al-Hakam, from Abu 'Iyad, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning ...﴾ to His saying ﴿and when you enter the afternoon﴾, he said: "The prayers were gathered: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾ is Maghrib and 'Isha', ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ is the Subh prayer, ﴿and at night﴾ is the 'Asr prayer, ﴿and when you enter the afternoon﴾ is the Zuhr prayer."

Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾ is Maghrib and 'Isha', ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ is Fajr, ﴿and at night﴾ is 'Asr, ﴿and when you enter the afternoon﴾ is Zuhr, and every prostration in the Qur'an is a prayer.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening﴾ is for the Maghrib prayer, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ is for the Subh prayer, ﴿and at night﴾ is for the 'Asr prayer, ﴿and when you enter the afternoon﴾ is the Zuhr prayer: four prayers.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, and to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you enter the afternoon﴾: "﴿When you enter the evening﴾ is the Maghrib prayer, ﴿and when you enter the morning﴾ is the Subh prayer, and at night is the 'Asr prayer, and when you enter the afternoon is the Zuhr prayer."

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living, and gives life to the earth after its death. And thus you will be brought forth.﴾ (30:19)

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Pray at these times which I have commanded you to pray at, O people. God is the One who brings the living out of the dead, that is, a living human being out of lifeless water, and brings lifeless water out of a living human being. ﴿And gives life to the earth after its death﴾ by making it grow plants, and brings forth its crops after its ruin and barrenness. ﴿And thus you will be brought forth﴾ means: just as He gives life to the earth after its death, bringing forth its vegetation and crops, so He will give you life after your death, bringing you out alive from your graves to the place of reckoning.

We have already explained, before the interpretation of His words ﴿He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living﴾, and mentioned the differences of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) concerning it. That is sufficient, so we will not repeat it here. However, we will mention some of the reports that we did not mention there, God willing.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 20–21:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].﴾ (30:20)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And among His proofs that He is capable of what He wills, O people, of bringing into being and annihilating, and of creating and destroying, and that every existing thing is created in the manner of your father, is that He made you from dust, meaning by this the creation of Adam from dust. He described them as having been created from dust, since that was His act upon their father Adam, in the manner we have already explained earlier in the discourse of the Arabs, where one addresses people with what was done to their predecessors, saying: "We did this to you, and we did that to you."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then, behold, you are human beings dispersing [throughout the earth]﴾

He says: Then, when you, the community of the offspring of the one whom We created from dust, are ﴿human beings dispersing﴾, He says: you move about and go in various directions.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust﴾: the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, from dust; ﴿then, behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾: meaning his descendants.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ (30:21)

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And among His proofs and evidences of this, also, is His creating for your father Adam a wife from his own self, so that he might find tranquility in her. This is because He created Eve from a rib of Adam's ribs.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves﴾: He created them for you from one of his ribs.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And He placed between you affection and mercy﴾

He says: He placed between you, through marriage and circumcision-related kinship (al-khutunah, i.e., relations by marriage), affection by which you show love to one another and maintain ties for its sake, and ﴿mercy﴾ by which He had mercy upon you, so that some of you incline toward others through it. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought﴾: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed in His doing that are lessons and admonitions for a people who reflect upon the proofs and evidences of God, so that they know that He is the God whom nothing He wills can overpower, and for whom no act He wishes is beyond reach.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And among His signs, He shows you the lightning, for fear and for hope﴾: "Fear for the traveller, and hope for the one who is resident."

Concerning the omission of "an" (that, the particle) in His saying ﴿He shows you the lightning﴾, the grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya, the scholars of Arabic) differed. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "It is not mentioned here, because this indicates the meaning," and a poet said:

*Alā ayyuhādhā al-zājirī uḥḍura al-waghā*
*wa an ashhada al-ladhdhāti hal anta mukhlidī*

[The line is by Tarafa ibn al-'Abd al-Bakri from his Mu'allaqa (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 317). In the Basran reading the verb is *uḥḍura* in the nominative, because when *an* is elided its government is lost, since in their view it does not govern when elided except in ten specific positions. In the Kufan reading it is *uḥḍura* in the accusative, because although it is elided, it is as though present due to the strength of the indication of it; so it is as though he said: *an uḥḍura*. *Al-wagha* means war, and its root is the sounds of the combatants in it. He says: "O you who rebuke me for witnessing war and pursuing pleasures, will you make me immortal in this world if I refrain from war?" And God, exalted is He, saying ﴿And among His signs, He shows you the lightning﴾ etc.: either ﴿among His signs﴾ is connected to ﴿He shows you﴾, so that it is in the accusative position, with *min* indicating the starting point; or ﴿He shows you﴾ is with *an* elided, as Tarafa said: "Alā ayyuhādhā..." (the line) with the nominative *uḥḍura*, as in the Basran reading. The estimate is: *an uḥḍura*. When *an* is omitted, the verb takes the nominative, so the estimate becomes: ﴿And among His signs, your being shown the lightning﴾.]

He said, and he said:

*Law qultu mā fī qawmihā lam yathīm*
*yafḍuluhā fī ḥasabin wa mīsami*

[The line is in rajaz meter by Hakim ibn Ma'iyya al-Rab'i al-Tamimi, an Islamic-era rajaz poet of the time of al-'Ajjaj; Sibawayh attributes it to him in his *Kitab* (Khizanat al-Adab al-Kubra of al-Baghdadi, 2:311). Al-Farra' recited it in his *Ma'ani al-Qur'an* in explaining God's words ﴿from those who are Jews, they distort words﴾, in one of two readings, and this is from the speech of the Arabs: they conceal *man* (with a fatha on the mim) in the beginning of a statement, as against *min* (with a kasra on the mim), and they say: *minnā yaqūlu dhālika wa minnā lā yaqūluhu* ("some of us say that and some of us do not say it"). This is because *min* with the kasra indicates a part of that to which it belongs, and so it conveys the omitted meaning. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾ and ﴿There is none of you but will come to it﴾. It is not permissible to omit *man* with a fatha in any of the descriptive or prepositional constructions except in this way which I have mentioned to you; the poet has used it with *fī* but I do not like it: "If I said what there is among her people, none would surpass her in lineage and beauty." It is permissible for you because you find in *min* with a kasra the sense of being a part of what it is attached to. Do you not see that you say: "Among us are the righteous, and among us are those less than that," so it is as though you said *minnā*. Al-Farra' said regarding God's saying ﴿And among His signs, He shows you the lightning﴾: "Whoever elides *an*, it is in the position of a nominative noun, as He said ﴿And among His signs, your sleep﴾. When you omit *an*, you make *min* with the kasra indicate an omitted noun, of which the verb is the relative clause, as in the poet's saying: 'Time is nothing but two occasions, so among them I die, and another I strive to seek life'," as though he meant: "among them an hour in which I die, and an hour in which I live." Likewise: ﴿And among His signs a sign of the lightning, and a sign of such-and-such.' And if you wish: ﴿He shows you from His signs the lightning﴾, then do not elide *an* or anything else." End of quotation.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 26–27:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [30:26] ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [30:27].

His exalted remembrance says: whoever is in the heavens and the earth, of angels, jinn and humans, are servants and possessions. ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ means: all are obedient to Him. Someone may say: how is it said ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ when it is known that most of mankind and jinn are disobedient to Him? We say: the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this, so we will mention their differences, then clarify the correct view among them on this matter. Some of them said: this is speech that is expressed in general terms, but what is intended is specific, and its meaning is: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ in life, subsistence, death, extinction, resurrection and rising, none of which anything can resist, even if some of them disobey Him in other matters.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and earth stand by His command...﴾ up to ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾, he said: means: obedient, referring to life, resurrection and death, while they are disobedient to Him in what is other than that, namely worship.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ by their acknowledgment that He is their Lord and Creator.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾: i.e., obedient, acknowledging that Allah is their Lord and Creator.

Others said: it is specific, and the meaning is: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, of angels and servants, the believer who is obedient to Allah, to the exclusion of others.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾: all are obedient to Him; the obedient one is the qanit. He said: there is nothing but that it is obedient, except the son of Adam, and he was most deserving of being the most obedient to Allah. And regarding His saying: ﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [2:238].

He said: this refers to prayer. Do not speak in prayer, as the People of the Book speak in prayer. He said: the People of the Book walk to one another during prayer. He said: they face one another during prayer, and when they are asked about that, they say: so that the rancour may leave our hearts and the hearts of some of us may submit to others. So Allah said: stand before Allah devoutly obedient, do not shift as they shift. Devoutly obedient: do not speak as they speak. He said: as for all other instances of qunut in the Qur'an, it means obedience, except this one.

The most correct of these views is the one we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, namely that everything in the heavens and the earth, being a creature of Allah, is obedient to His disposal of it according to what His exalted remembrance wills, of life, death and what resembles them, even if it disobeys Him in what it earns by its speech, and in what it has the way to choose and prefer over its opposite.

I only said that this is more correct in the interpretation of this, because the disobedient among His creatures in what they have the way to acquire is numerous, and He, exalted is His remembrance, has informed about all of them that they are devoutly obedient to Him. It is not permissible to inform that one who is disobedient is devoutly obedient to Him in that in which he is disobedient. Since that is the case, what they are disobedient in is what I have described, and what they are devoutly obedient in is what I have explained.

* *

His saying: ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it﴾

His exalted remembrance says: He to whom these attributes belong, blessed and exalted, is the One who originates creation from no prior source, brings it into being and causes it to exist after it was not a thing, then extinguishes it afterward, then repeats it, just as He originated it after its extinction, and ﴿that is easier for Him﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿that is easier for Him﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: it is easy for Him.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Wakī' related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Attar related to us, from Sufyan, from one he mentioned, from Mundhir al-Thawri, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym regarding ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾, he said: nothing is difficult for Him.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾, he said: everything is easy for Him.

Others said: its meaning is: the repetition of creation after their extinction is easier for Him than the beginning of their creation.

Mention of those who said this:

'Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾, he said: it means: easier for Him.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾, he said: the repetition is easier for Him than the initiation, and the initiation is easy for Him.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, that he recited this word: ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾, and said: the disbelievers were astonished at Allah's giving life to the dead. He said: then this verse was revealed: ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾, the repetition of creation is easier for Him than the origination of creation.

Ibn Wakī' related to us, he said: Ghundar related to us, from Shu'bah, from Simak, from Ikrimah, similarly, except that he said: the repetition of creation is easier for Him than its beginning.

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿and that is easier for Him﴾: he said: its repetition is easier for Him than its beginning, and everything is easy for Allah. In some readings: ﴿and everything is easy for Allah﴾.

This statement may bear two meanings other than the two views I mentioned, namely that its meaning is: It is He who originates creation then repeats it, and it is easier for the creatures; i.e., the repetition of a thing is easier for creatures than its initiation. And what we mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas in the report that Ibn Sa'd related to me is also a view with a valid basis.

as meaning: "khadi'" (submissive). And another's saying:

as meaning: "mighty, tall."

His saying: ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾

His exalted remembrance says: He is the Exalted in His vengeance against His enemies, the Wise in His management of His creatures and His disposal of them in what He wills of giving life, causing death, resurrection, rising, and whatever He wishes.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 26–27:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [30:26] ﴿It is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [30:27].

His exalted remembrance says: whoever is in the heavens and the earth, of angels, jinn and humans, are servants and possessions. ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ means: all are obedient to Him. Someone may say: how is it said ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ when it is known that most of mankind and jinn are disobedient to Him? We say: the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this, so we will mention their differences, then clarify the correct view among them on this matter. Some of them said: this is speech that is expressed in general terms, but what is intended is specific, and its meaning is: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ in life, subsistence, death, extinction, resurrection and rising, none of which anything can resist, even if some of them disobey Him in other matters.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and earth stand by His command...﴾ up to ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾, he said: means: obedient, referring to life, resurrection and death, while they are disobedient to Him in what is other than that, namely worship.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ by their acknowledgment that He is their Lord and Creator.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾: i.e., obedient, acknowledging that Allah is their Lord and Creator.

Others said: it is specific, and the meaning is: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, of angels and servants, the believer who is obedient to Allah, to the exclusion of others.

He said: there is nothing but that it is obedient, except the son of Adam, and he was most deserving of being the most obedient to Allah. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 28:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves: do you have, among what your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear one another?﴾ Thus We detail the signs for a people who reason.

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: He has set forth for you, O people, your Lord as a parable drawn from yourselves: ﴿Do you have, from what your right hands possess, [any] partners⁠—among those whom We have provided for you of wealth⁠—so that you are equal in it?﴾ He means: from your slaves, partners in what We have provided you of wealth, such that you are equal with them in it. He means: if you do not accept that for yourselves, how is it that you are pleased that your gods, whom you worship, be partners to Me in your worship of Me, while you and they are My servants and My slaves, and I am the owner of all of you?

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves: do you have, among what your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein﴾. He said: It is a parable God struck for whoever is made equal to Him in any of His creation. He says: Would any of you make your slave a partner with you in your bed and your wife?! Likewise, God does not accept that anyone of His creation be made equal to Him.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿He has coined for you a parable from yourselves: do you have, among what your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein﴾. He said: Do you find anyone who makes his slave like this in his wealth? How, then, do you, while you testify that they are My slaves and My creation, make for them a share in My worship? How could this be? He said: This is a parable God struck for them, and he recited: ﴿Thus We detail the signs for a people who reason﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿fearing them as you fear one another﴾. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: you fear these partners, from among what your right hands possess, that they might inherit your wealth after your death, just as some of you inherit from others.

Mention of those who said that:

It was reported to me from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "About the gods"; and concerning them He says: you fear they will inherit from you just as some of you inherit from one another.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: you fear these partners, from among what your right hands possess, that they will divide your wealth with you, just as some of you divide with one another.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Imran say: Abu Mijlaz said: "Your slave, you do not fear that he will share your wealth with you, and he has no right to that; likewise God has no partner."

The second of the two opinions is closer to the truth in the interpretation of this, because it better fits what the apparent meaning of the speech indicates. God, may His majesty be praised, rebuked these polytheists who make for Him, from among His creation, gods that they worship and associate with Him in their worship, while they nevertheless acknowledge that these are His creation and His slaves. He said to them: Do you have, from among your slaves, partners in what We have bestowed upon you of Our blessings, such that they are equal, and you fear in that they will divide with you that wealth which is between you and them, just as some of you fear that the one with whom he has a partnership in wealth will divide it? The fear that He, may He be exalted in remembrance, mentioned is more fitting as fear of what a partner fears from his partner dividing the wealth shared between them, than as fear that he will inherit from him; because mention of partnership does not indicate fear of inheritance, whereas it does indicate fear of separation and division.

And His words: ﴿Thus We detail the signs for a people who reason﴾.

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: Just as We have made clear to you, O people, Our proofs in these verses of this surah regarding Our power over what We will, creating what We will, annihilating what We love, and restoring what We wish to restore after its annihilation, and have shown that worship is fitting only for the One, the Subduer, in whose hand is the dominion of everything, so do We make clear Our proofs in every truth for a people who reason, who ponder them when they hear them and take heed, so that they are admonished by them.

The Commentary of Al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 30, Verse 29:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿But those who did wrong follow their desires without knowledge. So who can guide those whom Allah has led astray? For them there are no helpers.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: It is not so, and these polytheists did not associate the gods and idols in the worship of Allah, because they have partners in what Allah has provided them of their right hands' possessions, so they and their slaves are equal in it, fearing that they would share with them what their partners share in. Therefore, for Allah they approved what they approved for themselves, and so they associated them in His worship. But those who wronged themselves, disbelieved in Allah, and followed their desires out of ignorance of the right that Allah has over them, associating the gods and idols in His worship. ﴿So who can guide those whom Allah has led astray?﴾ He says: who will guide to the right path, meaning by that, who will grant success to Islam for one whom Allah has led astray from uprightness and right guidance? ﴿For them there are no helpers.﴾ He says: and for those whom Allah has led astray there are no helpers who could help them, so as to rescue them from the misguidance with which He, the Exalted, tests them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 30:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, the fitrah (natural disposition) of Allah upon which He has created mankind. No change is there in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know﴾ (30)

He, the Exalted, says: So direct your face toward the religion toward which your Lord has directed you, O Muhammad, to obey Him, and it is the religion (al-din). ﴿Hanifan﴾ means: upright in His religion and His obedience. ﴿The fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾ means: the creation of Allah upon which He created people. "Fitrah" is put in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) from the meaning of His saying, ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth﴾, because the meaning is: Allah created people upon that as a fitrah.

The exegetes have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying, ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾: It is Islam, since Allah created them all from Adam, acknowledging this. And he recited: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify"﴾. He said: This is the saying of Allah: ﴿Mankind was one community, and Allah sent the prophets﴾ afterward.

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿the fitrah of Allah﴾: He said: Islam.

* Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Salih told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, who said: Umar passed by Mu'adh ibn Jabal and said: What is the foundation (qiwam) of this Ummah? Mu'adh said: Three, and they are the saviours: sincerity (ikhlas), which is the fitrah ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾; prayer, which is the religion (milla); and obedience, which is protection (ismah). Umar said: You have spoken truly.

* Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told me, saying: Ayyub told us, from Abu Qilabah, that Umar said to Mu'adh: What is the foundation of this Ummah? Then he mentioned something similar.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾

It means: there is no alteration of the religion of Allah; that is, that is not right, and it should not be done.

The exegetes differed in its interpretation. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: He said: for His religion.

* Abu al-Sa'ib told me, saying: Ibn Idris told us, from Layth, who said: Mujahid sent a man called Qasim to Ikrimah to ask him about the saying of Allah: ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾. It is only the religion, and he recited: ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion﴾.

* Ibn Wakic told us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab told us, from Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, concerning ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind﴾: He said: Islam.

He said: My father told me, from Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, concerning ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: He said: for the religion of Allah.

He said: My father told me, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: for the religion of Allah.

* He said: My father told us, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ward, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: Mujahid said: Ask Ikrimah about it. I asked him, and Ikrimah said: The religion of Allah the Exalted, what is wrong with him, may Allah disgrace him?! Has he not heard His saying: ﴿the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind; no change is there in the creation of Allah﴾?

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: that is, for the religion of Allah.

* Ibn Wakic told us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, from Layth, from Ikrimah, who said: for the religion of Allah.

* He said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, from Humayd al-A'raj, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: for the religion of Allah.

* He said: al-Muharibi told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: for the religion of Allah.

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: the religion of Allah.

* Ibn Wakic told us, saying: My father told us, from Mis'ar and Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ibrahim, who said: ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾: for the religion of Allah.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Wakic told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Mutarrif, from a man, who asked Ibn Abbas about the castration of animals; he disliked it and said: ﴿No change is there in the creation of Allah﴾.

* He said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, from Humayd al-A'raj, who said: Ikrimah said: It is castration.

* He said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: It is castration.

* * *

And His saying: ﴿That is the correct religion﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Your setting your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, unaltered and unchanged, is the correct religion, meaning: the straight one with no deviation from uprightness (istiqamah) through hanifiyyah to Judaism, Christianity, and other misguidance and innovated heresies.

Some of them directed the meaning of "religion" in this place to mean "the reckoning".

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Amarah told me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Musa told us, saying: Abu Layla informed us, from Buraydah, concerning ﴿That is the correct religion﴾: He said: the correct reckoning.

﴿But most of the people do not know﴾: He, the Exalted, says: But most people do not know that the religion I have commanded you, O Muhammad, by My saying ﴿So set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth﴾ is the true religion, to the exclusion of all other religions besides it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 31–32:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Turning penitently to Him, and be mindful of Him, and establish prayer, and be not among the polytheists﴾ [30:31], ﴿Of those who split up their religion and became sects, each faction rejoicing in what they have﴾ [30:32].

By His words ﴿turning penitently to Him﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: repentant, returning to God, turning towards Him.

As related:

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿turning penitently to Him﴾: "The one who turns penitently to God is the one who obeys God, who has turned to obedience to God and His command, and has returned from the matters in which he was before that. The people were disbelievers, then they desisted and returned to Islam."

The meaning of the statement is: So set your face, O Muhammad, toward the religion as a ḥanīf, ﴿turning penitently to Him﴾, to God. So "al-munībūn" (those who turn penitently) is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of the kāf in "your face."

If someone says: How can it be a circumstantial qualifier of it, when the kāf refers to one person, while "al-munībūn" is a description of a group? It is said: Because the command addressed to the kāf is, in this place, a command from Him addressed to him and to his community. So it is as if it were said to him: So set your face, you and your community, toward the religion as ḥanīf for God, turning penitently to Him.

* *

As for His words ﴿and be mindful of Him﴾:

He, may His majesty be praised, says: Fear God and watch over Him, lest you fall short in His obedience and commit His disobedience. ﴿And be not among the polytheists﴾ means: And do not be among the people of polytheism toward God by neglecting His obligations, committing His acts of disobedience, and opposing the religion to which He has called you.

* *

As for His words ﴿Of those who split up their religion and became sects﴾:

He says: Do not be among the polytheists who changed their religion, opposed it, and separated from it, ﴿and became sects﴾, meaning: and became factions and divisions, like the Jews and the Christians.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿those who split up their religion and became sects﴾: they are the Jews and the Christians.

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿those who split up their religion and became sects﴾ to the end of the verse: "These are the Jews." Then, if His words ﴿Of those who split up their religion﴾ were directed as a separate, new statement, detached from His words ﴿and be not among the polytheists﴾, and its meaning were: ﴿of those who split up their religion and became sects﴾, factions, ﴿each faction rejoicing in what they have﴾, that would be a possible reading that the wording allows.

* *

As for His words ﴿each faction rejoicing in what they have﴾:

He says: Every group and sect of those who departed from the true religion, and innovated the innovations they introduced, ﴿rejoicing in what they have﴾, meaning: rejoicing and pleased with the school of thought to which they hold fast, supposing that the right course is with them and not with others.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 33–35:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And when harm touches mankind, they call upon their Lord, turning in repentance to Him. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, at once a party of them associate others with their Lord,﴾ (33)

Says God, may He be remembered: When harm, i.e. hardship, drought and famine, touches these polytheists who set up another god alongside God, ﴿they call upon their Lord﴾, i.e. they devote their worship to their Lord alone, single Him out for supplication and humble entreaty, and seek His help, ﴿turning in repentance to Him﴾, repenting to Him from their polytheism and disbelief. ﴿Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him﴾, i.e. when their Lord, may He be remembered, removes that harm from them, relieves them of it, and grants them prosperity, abundance and plenty, ﴿at once a party of them﴾, i.e. at once a group of them, ﴿associate others with their Lord﴾, i.e. they worship alongside Him the gods and idols.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So that they may deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ (34)

Says God, may He be remembered, threatening these polytheists of whom He has informed that when He removes harm from them they disbelieve in Him: "So that they deny what We have given them", i.e. when they associate others with their Lord, [they do so] so that they may deny [the] blessing We have bestowed upon them by removing from them the harm they were in and replacing it for them with prosperity, plenty and well-being. That prosperity and abundance is what He, may He be remembered, gave them. His words ﴿what We have given them﴾ refer to that. His words ﴿So enjoy yourselves﴾ mean: so enjoy, O people, what We have given you of prosperity and abundance in this world, ﴿for you will soon know﴾, when you come before your Lord, what punishment you will meet from Him and the great severity of His retribution for your disbelief in Him in this world.

Some readers recited ﴿fa-sawfa yaʿlamūn﴾ (for they will soon know) with the ya' (third person), meaning: "that they may deny what We have given them, so they have enjoyed themselves" is stated as a report, "so they will soon know."

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they associate?﴾ (35)

Says God, may He be remembered: Or have We sent down to those who associate others in worship with Us, gods and idols, a book confirming what they say and the truth of what they do? ﴿So that it speaks of what they associate﴾, i.e. that book speaks to the validity of their polytheism. What He, may He be exalted, means by this is: He has not sent down any book for what they say and do, nor sent any messenger with it; rather it is something they invented and fabricated, following their own desires.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they associate﴾, he said: "Or have We sent down to them a book, so that it speaks of their polytheism."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 36:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it. But if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have put forward, then they are despairing﴾ [30:36].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: when We grant people fertility, ease, and well-being in their bodies and wealth, they rejoice at that. And if We afflict them with hardship, through drought, famine, and calamity in their wealth and bodies, ﴿because of what their hands have put forward﴾, meaning: because of the evil deeds they have sent ahead between themselves and God, and the sins they have committed. ﴿then they are despairing﴾, meaning: they then despair of relief. Al-qunut (despair) is al-iyas (hopelessness), and from it comes the verse of Humayd al-Arqat:

"They found al-Hajjaj not despairing [of rain]..." [[The line is by Humayd al-Arqat (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, folio 188b), who said: "(iza huwa yaqnatun): that is, they despair." Humayd al-Arqat said: "They have found ... " the line. In (Lisan al-Arab, root q-n-t): al-qunut is al-yas (despair). In (al-Tahdhib): despair of good. It is also said: intense despair of something. Qanata yaqnutu and yaqnitu (as daraba and nasara) and qanita qanatan as ta'iba, so he is qanit (despairing). It has been read: ﴿and do not be of those who despair﴾ [15:55]. As for qanata yaqnutu (with fatha in both) and qanita yaqnitu (with kasra in both), they are a combination of the two dialects, as al-Akhfash said.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿then they are despairing﴾

This is the response of the conditional (jawab al-jaza'), because "idha" (then/when) stands in for the verb through its indication of it. It is as if it were said: "and if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have put forward, you will find them despairing," or "you will find them," or "you will see them," or "you will see them [despairing]." Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say that "idha" serves as the response because it is connected to the first clause, in the position of the fa' (so).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 37–39:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ (30:37)

His exalted remembrance says: Have these people not seen, with the eyes of their hearts, those who rejoice when prosperity and abundance reach them, and who despair of relief when hardship befalls them, so that they would know that hardship and ease are in the hand of Allah, and that Allah extends provision to whom He wills among His servants, widening it for him, and restricts it for whom He wishes, narrowing it for him? ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ means: in His extending it to whom He extends it, and His restricting it for whom He restricts it, and His varying between those among His servants whom He varies between in wealth and poverty, there is a clear proof for whoever affirms the proofs of Allah and acknowledges them when he witnesses and sees them.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So give to the near of kin his right, and to the needy and the wayfarer. That is better for those who seek the Face of Allah, and those are the successful.﴾ (30:38)

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So give, O Muhammad, to the kinsman his right over you of kinship and goodness, and to the needy and the wayfarer what Allah has obligated for them in that.

As:

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan, concerning ﴿So give to the near of kin his right, and to the needy and the wayfarer﴾: he said, "It is that you pay them their rights if you have ease; and if you do not have it, then say to them a gentle word, speak to them good."

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is better for those who seek the Face of Allah﴾

His exalted remembrance says: giving these their rights, which Allah has imposed upon His servants, is better for those who seek Allah by giving them that. ﴿And those are the successful﴾ means: whoever does that seeking the Face of Allah by it, those are the achievers, who attain their aims with Allah, who succeed in what they sought and desired by giving them what they gave.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people—it does not increase with Allah. But what you give in zakah, seeking the Face of Allah—those are the multipliers.﴾ (30:39)

His exalted remembrance says: And whatever you give, O people, to one another by way of gifts, so that it may increase in people's wealth through the return of its reward to you from the one to whom you gave it, ﴿it does not increase with Allah﴾, meaning: that does not increase with Allah, because its giver did not give it seeking His Face. ﴿And what you give in zakah﴾ means: what you give in charity, seeking by it the Face of Allah. ﴿Those﴾ refers to those who give their wealth, seeking by it the Face of Allah. ﴿They are the multipliers﴾ means: they are those who have multiplication of reward and recompense. From the saying of the Arabs: "The people became ones whose camels are fat and thirsty (musmiʿīn muʿṭishīn)," when their camels became fat and thirsty.

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So give, O Muhammad, to the kinsman his right over you of kinship and goodness, and to the needy and the wayfarer what Allah has obligated for them in that.

⁕ Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Mughīrah, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning ﴿And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people﴾: he said, "Have you not seen a man who says to another, 'I will enrich you,' and so gives him? This does not increase with Allah, because he gives it to other than Allah in order to increase his wealth."

⁕ He said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Āmilī narrated to us, saying: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī say concerning His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah﴾: "This was in the Jāhiliyyah; one of them would give his relative wealth so that his own wealth might increase."

Others said: That is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ), while for others it is permissible.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Abū Rawwād, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, concerning ﴿And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah﴾: "This is for the Prophet (ﷺ); this is the permissible usury."

We chose the view we have chosen only because it is the most apparent of its meanings.

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra and some of the people of Mecca read ﴿li-yarbū﴾ with a fatḥah on the yāʾ from yarbū, meaning: "and whatever you give in usury, so that that usury may increase within people's wealth." The majority of the reciters of Medina read ﴿li-tarbū﴾ with a tāʾ from tarbū and a ḍammah on it, meaning: "and whatever you give in usury, so that you may increase within people's wealth."

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known readings among the reciters of the regional centres, with their meanings closely related; for when the owners of wealth make wealth increase, it increases through their making it increase; and when wealth increases, it increases through the increasing of its owners. Given this, whichever of the two readings the reader recites is correct.

As for His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in zakah, seeking the Face of Allah—those are the multipliers﴾, the people of interpretation said concerning its explanation the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, concerning His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in zakah, seeking the Face of Allah—those are the multipliers﴾: "This is what Allah accepts, and He multiplies it for them tenfold, and more than that."

⁕ Narrated to us from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said concerning His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah﴾: "It is the gift; one gives a thing desiring to be repaid with something better than it. That is what does not increase with Allah; its giver is not rewarded for it, and there is no sin upon him." ﴿And whatever you give in zakah﴾: "It is charity, seeking the Face of Allah." ﴿Those are the multipliers.﴾ Maʿmar said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid the like of that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 40–41:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the One Who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Is there any of your partners who does anything of that? Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate.﴾ (40)

He, exalted is His mention, says to the polytheists who associate others with Him, informing them of the ugliness of their deed and the wickedness of their conduct: "Allah, O people, is the One for whom worship is fitting and who should not be directed to anyone else. He is the One who created you when you were nothing, then provided for you and gave you what you possess, though you owned nothing before that. Then He causes you to die after having created you living, and then He gives you life again after your death, for the resurrection of the Last Day."

As Qatadah said: Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Allah is the One Who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life﴾: "for the resurrection after death."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Is there among your gods and idols, which you make partners with Allah in your worship of Him, any that does anything of that, by creating, or providing, or causing death, or raising up? This is a rebuke from Allah to these polytheists. The meaning of the speech is that their partners do none of that, so how can one be worshipped besides Allah when he does none of that? Then He, exalted is His mention, cleared Himself of the slander that these polytheists had invented against Him by claiming that their gods were His partners. So He, great is His praise, said: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is, exalting Allah and declaring Him free of imperfection, ﴿and high is He﴾, says: and exalted is He, ﴿above what they associate﴾, says: above the associating of these polytheists with Him.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Is there any of your partners who does anything of that?﴾ "No, by Allah." ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate﴾: He glorifies Himself when the slander is attributed to Him.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, that they might return.﴾ (41)

He, exalted is His mention, says: Sins have appeared on the land and sea through the earnings of people's hands, namely what Allah has forbidden them.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the intended meaning of His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾. Some of them said: By "the land" is meant the wastelands, and by "the sea" is meant the cities and villages situated on water and rivers.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Abu Kurayb, who said: Utham related to us, who said: al-Nadr ibn Arabi related to us, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein...﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: "When he turns away, he strives by transgression and injustice, so Allah withholds the rain, and so ﴿He destroys the crops and the progeny, and Allah does not love corruption.﴾" He said: Then Mujahid recited: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea...﴾ to the end of the verse, and he said: "Indeed, by Allah, it is not your sea of this kind, but every town on flowing water is a sea."

Narrated to us Ibn Wakie', who said: My father related to us, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾, he said: "Indeed, I do not say it is your sea of this kind, but every town on flowing water."

He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Amr ibn Furukh, from Habib ibn al-Zubayr, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾, he said: "The Arabs call cities 'seas'."

Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned﴾: He said: "This was before Allah sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ); it was filled with misguidance and injustice. Then when Allah sent His Prophet, those among the people who returned came back."

* *

His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾

As for the land, it is the people of the tents; as for the sea, it is the people of the towns and countryside.

Narrated to me Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾: "The sins." And he recited: ﴿that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, that they might return.﴾

Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Abu Amir related to us, who said: Qurrah related to us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned﴾: He said: "Allah corrupted them through their sins, in the sea and land of the earth, by their wicked deeds."

Others said: Rather, by "the land" is meant the surface of the earth, the cities and others, and by "the sea" is meant the well-known sea.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Ibn Wakie', who said: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾: He said: "On the land: the son of Adam who killed his brother; and in the sea: the one who used to seize every ship by force."

Narrated to me Ya'qub, who said: Abu Bishr—meaning Ibn Ulayyah—said: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea by what the hands of people have earned﴾: "By the killing of the son of Adam, and the one who used to seize every ship by force."

Narrated to us Ibn Wakie', who said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Atiyyah regarding ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land and the sea﴾: He said: "I said: This is the land; and the sea, what corruption is in it?" He said: "When the rain decreases, the pearl-diving decreases."

Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Corruption has appeared on the land﴾: He said: "The son of Adam killed his brother." ﴿And the sea﴾: He said: "The king seized the ships by force."

The most correct of these opinions in the view of truth is that Allah, great is His mention, informed that corruption has appeared on the land and the sea among the Arabs, in the barren lands; and the sea is of two kinds: salt sea and sweet water sea, and both are called "sea" by them. Allah, great is His praise, did not single out the report of its appearance in one sea rather than another, so it applies to whatever is called a sea, whether sweet or salt. Since that is so, it includes the towns situated on rivers and seas.

So the meaning of the speech, then, since the matter is as you have described, is that the disobedience of Allah appeared in every place, land and sea, ﴿by what the hands of people have earned﴾, that is, through people's sins, and injustice spread in both.

* *

His saying: ﴿that He may let them taste part of that which they have done﴾

He, great is His praise, says: that He may afflict them with the punishment for some of their deeds that they did and their disobedience that they committed, ﴿that they might return﴾, that is: that they may turn back to the truth, repent, and abandon the disobedience of Allah.

The people of interpretation have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Narrated to us Ibn Wakie', who said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan regarding ﴿that they might return﴾: He said: "They repent."

He said: Ibn Mahdi related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah regarding ﴿that they might return﴾: "On the day of Badr, that perhaps they would repent."

He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Ibrahim regarding ﴿that they might return﴾: He said: "To the truth."

Narrated to us Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿that He may let them taste part of that which they have done, that they might return﴾: "Perhaps one returning will return, perhaps one repenting will repent, perhaps one seeking to be pleased will be pleased."

Narrated to us Ibn Bashshar, who said: Abu Amir related to us, who said: Qurrah related to us, from al-Hasan regarding ﴿that they might return﴾: He said: "Those after them will return."

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿li-yudhīqahum﴾ (that He may let them taste). The majority of the readers of the cities recited ﴿li-yudhīqahum﴾ with the letter ya', meaning: that Allah may let them taste some of what they did. It is mentioned that Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami recited it with the letter nun, as a report from Allah about Himself.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 42–43:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and see how was the end of those before you. Most of them were polytheists."﴾ (42)

Allah, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people who associate others with Allah: Travel through the lands and look at the dwellings of those who disbelieved in Allah before you and denied His messengers, and see what was the final outcome for them, and the consequence of their denial of the messengers of Allah and their disbelief. Did We not destroy them with a punishment from Us, and make them a lesson for those who came after them? ﴿Most of them were polytheists﴾ means: We did that to them because most of them were polytheists, associating others with Allah just as you do.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion, before there comes from Allah a Day which cannot be turned back. That Day they will be divided.﴾ (43)

Allah, may He be remembered, says: So turn your face, O Muhammad, toward the direction to which your Lord has directed you, (toward the upright religion) for the obedience of your Lord, and the straight path that has no deviation from the truth. ﴿Before there comes from Allah a Day which cannot be turned back﴾ means: before the coming of a day from the days of Allah which cannot be averted when it comes, because Allah has decreed its coming, so it will certainly come. ﴿That Day they will be divided﴾ means: on the day that day comes, people will be divided, that is, separated into two groups, from the expression of the Arabs: "I divided the sheep into two flocks (ṣadaʿtu al-ghanama ṣadʿatayn)" when I separated them into two groups: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾, the upright religion being Islam, ﴿before there comes from Allah a Day which cannot be turned back. That Day they will be divided﴾: a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿That Day they will be divided﴾: he said: they will separate.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿They will be divided﴾: he said: they will separate, some to Paradise and some to the Fire.
