**Commentary on the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of meaning) of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief, and whoever does righteous deeds, for themselves they prepare (a resting place)﴾ (30:44)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: whoever disbelieves in God, upon him are the burdens of his disbelief and the sins of his denial of his Lord's bounties. ﴿And whoever does righteousness﴾ means: whoever obeys God, doing what He commanded him in this world and refraining from what He forbade him in it. ﴿For themselves they prepare﴾ means: for themselves they make ready and smooth the bed, so that they may be safe from the punishment of their Lord and be saved from His chastisement, as the poet said:

*Prepare for yourself before sickness and death draw near,*
*and do not waste a soul that has no successor.*

(The verse is attributed to Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Adawi. Abu 'Ubayda, in his Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 189a, said in explaining His words "fa-li-anfusihim yamhadun": "man" (with a fatha on the mim) applies to the singular, the dual and the plural, and its figurative usage here is the plural usage. "Yamhadu" means he earns, works and prepares. Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Adawi said: "Prepare for yourself..." The verse. "Hann" means "drew near," and "al-talaf" means death. In Lisan al-'Arab, under (m-h-d), it says: "He prepared for himself (yamhudu mahdan, like fataha), meaning he earned and worked.")

Those among the people of ta'wil (the early exegetes) said things similar to what we have said regarding its interpretation.

**Those who said so:**

- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿For themselves they prepare﴾: he said, "They make the beds ready."

- Ibn al-Muthanna, al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan, Ibn Wakī', and Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-'Alai narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿For themselves they prepare﴾: he said, "In the grave."

- Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿For themselves they prepare﴾: he said, "For the grave."

- Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, saying: I heard Mujahid say regarding His words ﴿For themselves they prepare﴾: "In the grave."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 45–46:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾ (45)

Exalted is His remembrance says: ﴿On that Day they will be separated...﴾ ﴿That He may reward those who believe﴾ in Allah and His Messenger ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: and act in accordance with what Allah has commanded them ﴿out of His bounty﴾, which He promised to whoever obeyed Him in this world, that He would reward them on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.﴾ Exalted is His remembrance says: He singled out for His reward out of His bounty those who believe and do righteous deeds, rather than those who disbelieve in Allah; indeed, He does not love the people of disbelief in Him. He began a new statement with His words, ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers,﴾ and it contains the meaning you have described.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as bringers of good tidings, and that He may let you taste of His mercy, and that the ships may sail by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ (46)

Exalted is His remembrance says: Among the proofs of His oneness and His arguments against you, that He is the God of everything, ﴿is that He sends the winds as bringers of good tidings﴾ with rain and mercy, ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, meaning: and that He may send down upon you of His mercy, which is the rain by which He gives life to the lands, and that the ships may sail upon the seas by His command to them, ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: and that you may seek of His provisions and livelihoods which He has apportioned among you, ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾, meaning: and that you may thank your Lord for that. He sent these winds as bringers of good tidings.

The people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the winds as bringers of good tidings﴾, he said: with rain.

And they said regarding His saying, ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, the same as what we have said about it.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, he said: the rain.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾: the rain.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 47:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We had already sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We took vengeance upon those who committed crime, and it was due upon Us to aid the believers.﴾ (30:47)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, consoling His Prophet ﷺ regarding what he suffers of harm from his people, by what was suffered by the messengers before him from their peoples, and informing him of His practice concerning them and their peoples, and that He is proceeding with him and his people according to His practice concerning them and their nations: "And We had already sent, O Muhammad, messengers before you to their peoples, the disbelievers, just as We sent you to your people who worship idols besides Allah." ﴿Then they came to them with clear proofs﴾ meaning: with evident proofs of their truthfulness and that they were messengers of Allah, just as you came to your people with clear proofs, and they denied them, just as your people denied you, and they rejected what they brought them from Allah, just as they rejected from you what you brought them from your Lord. ﴿Then We took vengeance upon those who committed crime﴾ means: So We took vengeance upon those who committed sins and earned evil deeds from their peoples, and We will likewise do to the criminals of your people. ﴿And it was due upon Us to aid the believers﴾ means: And We delivered those who believed in Allah and affirmed His messengers when His punishment came to them, and thus We will do with you and with those among your people who believe in you. ﴿And it was due upon Us to aid the believers﴾ against the disbelievers, and We are your helpers and the helpers of those who believe in you against those who disbelieve in you, and We will grant you victory over them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 48:

Regarding the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, then He spreads them across the sky however He wills and breaks them into fragments, and you see the rain coming out from within them. Then when He causes it to fall upon whomever He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾, meaning: the winds bring into being clouds, the word being the plural of sahabah (a cloud). ﴿Then He spreads them across the sky however He wills﴾, meaning: Allah spreads them out and gathers them together in the sky however He wills. He said ﴿fa-yabsuṭuhu﴾ (then He spreads it), using the singular pronoun, and gave it the form of a masculine pronoun. The word "sahab" (clouds) is a collective noun, as I have described, and the pronoun refers back to the word "sahab" and not to its meaning, just as one says: "This is good dates" (tamr jayyid).

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿fa-yabsuṭuhu﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then He spreads it across the sky however He wills﴾: and gathers it together.

* *

And His words: ﴿and breaks it into fragments﴾

Meaning: and He makes the clouds into pieces, scattered.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and breaks it into fragments﴾: that is, pieces.

* *

And His words: ﴿then you see the rain﴾

Meaning: the rain ﴿coming out from within it﴾, meaning: from between the clouds.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then you see the rain coming out from within it﴾.

Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, from Qatn, from Habib, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, regarding ﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds﴾, he said: The winds are four. Allah sends a wind which sweeps the earth clean, then Allah sends the second wind which stirs up clouds, and He makes them into fragments in the sky; then Allah sends the third wind which joins them together and makes them into a heap; then He sends the fourth wind and it rains.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿then you see the rain﴾, he said: the rainfall.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then when He causes it to fall upon whomever He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice﴾

He says: When He turns that rain toward the land of whomever He wills of His creation, you see them rejoicing, that He has turned that rain toward them, and being glad.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 49–50:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And although, before it was sent down upon them, before it, they were certainly despairing﴾.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And these people whom Allah afflicted with this rain from among His servants, before this rain was sent down upon them, before this rain, were ﴿certainly despairing﴾, meaning: dejected and grieved, because it had been withheld from them.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And although, before it was sent down upon them, before it, they were certainly despairing﴾: i.e., despairing.

The scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) differed over the purpose of the repetition of "min qablihi" (before it), when the phrase "min qabli an yunzala 'alayhim" (before it was sent down upon them) had already been mentioned. Some grammarians of Basra said: the repetition of "min qablihi" is for emphasis (tawkid), like His words: ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾. Others said: it is not so, because "min qabli an yunzala 'alayhim" has a particle (harf) that the second does not have. He said: it is as if he said: "before the sending down, before the rain," so the two differ. As for ﴿kulluhum ajma'un﴾ (all of them together), it is emphasized with "ajma'un," because "kull" can be a noun and can also be an emphasis, and "ajma'un" is the emphasis. My view regarding His words ﴿min qablihi﴾ is that it is for emphasis.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the One who will give life to the dead, and He is over all things Omnipotent﴾.

The reciters differed over His words ﴿fanzur ila athari rahmati Allah﴾ (so look at the traces of Allah's mercy). The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿ila athari rahmati Allah﴾ (to the trace of Allah's mercy) in the singular, meaning: so look, O Muhammad, at the trace of the rain with which Allah afflicted whom He afflicted of His servants, how that rain gives life to the earth after its death. The majority of the reciters of Kufah recited ﴿fanzur ila athari rahmati Allah﴾ in the plural, meaning: so look at the traces of the rain with which Allah afflicted whom He afflicted, how He gives life to the earth after its death.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations in the recitation of the regional schools (amsar), close in meaning. That is because when Allah gives life to the earth by a rain He sends down upon it, the rain gives it life by Allah's giving it life through it; and when the rain gives it life, Allah is the One who gives life through it. So whichever of the two recitations the reader recites, he is correct. The meaning of the speech is therefore: so look, O Muhammad, at the traces of the rain that Allah sends down from the clouds, how by it He gives life to the dead earth, causing it to bring forth plants and vegetation, after its death and effacement. ﴿Indeed, that is the One who will give life to the dead﴾. He, majestic is His remembrance, says: indeed He who gives life to this earth after its death by this rain is the One who will give life to the dead after their death, and He is over all things, with His power to give life to the dead, Omnipotent; nothing He wills is beyond Him, and no act He wishes, glorified is He, is withheld from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 51–53:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow, they would surely continue after that in disbelief﴾ (51).

Exalted is He says: And if We sent a wind that corrupts what the rain We sent down from the sky had caused to grow, so that these people, to whom God gave, through that rain by which their lands were revived, and by which their plants turned green and their crops sprouted, see what their lands had produced of crops through that rain turned yellow, having been corrupted by that wind which We sent, so that it became yellow after its greenness, they would surely continue in disbelief in their Lord after their rejoicing and delight in it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating (52). Nor can you guide the blind out of their error. You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs, and they are Muslims (53).﴾

Exalted is He says: ﴿So indeed you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿cannot make the dead hear﴾, meaning: You cannot give them hearing by which they understand from you what you say to them. This is only an illustration of the meaning: You cannot make these polytheists understand, those upon whose hearing God has set a seal, depriving them of the understanding of the admonitions of His revelation that are recited to them, just as you cannot make the dead understand, whom God has deprived of their hearing, by giving them hearing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾

He means: Just as you cannot make the deaf, who have been deprived of hearing, hear the call when they turn away from you retreating, so too you cannot grant success to those whom God has deprived of understanding of the signs of His Book, so that they hear and understand it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾: This is an example God struck for the disbeliever: just as the dead does not hear the call, so the disbeliever does not hear. ﴿And nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾ means: if a deaf person turned away retreating and you called him, he would not hear; likewise the disbeliever does not hear, nor benefit from what he hears.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind out of their error﴾

Exalted is He says: And you, O Muhammad, are not one who guides to the right path him whom God has blinded from uprightness and the road of truth, so that He has not granted him success in attaining right guidance; you cannot turn him away from his error in which he is, and from his riding of the crooked paths to the way of rectitude. He means: that is not in your hand nor up to you, and no one can do that except Me, for I am capable of all things. It is said: ﴿guide the blind out of their error﴾ and it does not say "from their error" because the meaning of the speech is what I described, namely: you cannot turn them away from it; so it was construed according to the meaning. Had it said "from their error", it would have been correct, meaning: you cannot prevent them from their error.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs﴾

Exalted is He says to His Prophet: You cannot make hear the hearing by which the listener benefits and understands, except those who believe in Our signs, because whoever believes in Our signs, when he hears the Book of God, contemplates it, understands it, comprehends it, acts by what is in it, and stops at the limits of God which He set in it, he is the one who hears the beneficial hearing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they are Muslims﴾

He means: They are submissive to God in obeying Him, humbled before the admonitions of His Book.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 51–53:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turned yellow, they would surely continue after that in disbelief﴾ (51).

Exalted is He says: And if We sent a wind that corrupts what the rain We sent down from the sky had caused to grow, so that these people, to whom God gave, through that rain by which their lands were revived, and by which their plants turned green and their crops sprouted, see what their lands had produced of crops through that rain turned yellow, having been corrupted by that wind which We sent, so that it became yellow after its greenness, they would surely continue in disbelief in their Lord after their rejoicing and delight in it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating (52). Nor can you guide the blind out of their error. You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs, and they are Muslims (53).﴾

Exalted is He says: ﴿So indeed you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿cannot make the dead hear﴾, meaning: You cannot give them hearing by which they understand from you what you say to them. This is only an illustration of the meaning: You cannot make these polytheists understand, those upon whose hearing God has set a seal, depriving them of the understanding of the admonitions of His revelation that are recited to them, just as you cannot make the dead understand, whom God has deprived of their hearing, by giving them hearing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾

He means: Just as you cannot make the deaf, who have been deprived of hearing, hear the call when they turn away from you retreating, so too you cannot grant success to those whom God has deprived of understanding of the signs of His Book, so that they hear and understand it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾: This is an example God struck for the disbeliever: just as the dead does not hear the call, so the disbeliever does not hear. ﴿And nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾ means: if a deaf person turned away retreating and you called him, he would not hear; likewise the disbeliever does not hear, nor benefit from what he hears.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Nor can you guide the blind out of their error﴾

Exalted is He says: And you, O Muhammad, are not one who guides to the right path him whom God has blinded from uprightness and the road of truth, so that He has not granted him success in attaining right guidance; you cannot turn him away from his error in which he is, and from his riding of the crooked paths to the way of rectitude. He means: that is not in your hand nor up to you, and no one can do that except Me, for I am capable of all things. It is said: ﴿guide the blind out of their error﴾ and it does not say "from their error" because the meaning of the speech is what I described, namely: you cannot turn them away from it; so it was construed according to the meaning. Had it said "from their error", it would have been correct, meaning: you cannot prevent them from their error.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs﴾

Exalted is He says to His Prophet: You cannot make hear the hearing by which the listener benefits and understands, except those who believe in Our signs, because whoever believes in Our signs, when he hears the Book of God, contemplates it, understands it, comprehends it, acts by what is in it, and stops at the limits of God which He set in it, he is the one who hears the beneficial hearing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they are Muslims﴾

He means: They are submissive to God in obeying Him, humbled before the admonitions of His Book.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 54–55:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.﴾ (54)

His saying, the Exalted, addresses these deniers of the Resurrection among the polytheists of Quraysh, arguing against them that He is capable of this and of whatever He wills: ﴿Allah is the One who created you﴾, O people, ﴿from weakness﴾, meaning: from a drop of semen and despised water, then He brought you into being as a well-formed human. ﴿Then made after weakness strength﴾, meaning: then He gave you strength to act, after He created you from weakness and after your weakness through infancy and childhood. ﴿Then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾, meaning: then He brought upon you weakness through decrepitude and old age, after you had been strong in your youth, and gray hair.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿who created you from weakness﴾, i.e., from a drop of semen; ﴿then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness﴾, i.e., senility; ﴿and gray hair﴾, i.e., the grey of the temples (al-shamt).

* *

And His saying: ﴿He creates what He wills﴾

Meaning: He creates what He wills of weakness, strength, youth and gray hair. ﴿And He is the Knowing﴾ of the disposition of His creation, ﴿the Competent﴾ over whatever He wills; nothing He intends is beyond His ability. Just as He did these things, so He causes His creatures to die and revives them when He wills. Meaning: know that the One who did these deeds by His power can revive the dead when He wills.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they had not remained but an hour. Thus were they deluded.﴾ (55)

His saying, the Exalted: On the day when the moment of resurrection comes and creatures are raised from their graves, the criminals will swear, namely those who disbelieved in Allah in the world and earned sins therein. Their oath is their swearing by Allah: ﴿that they had not remained but an hour﴾, meaning: they will swear that they did not remain in their graves more than one hour. Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: thus in the world too they were deluded, meaning: they lied in their statement and oath, "We did not remain but an hour," just as they used to lie and swear falsely in the world while knowing it.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they had not remained but an hour. Thus were they deluded﴾: i.e., they lied in the world. What is meant by His saying ﴿were deluded﴾ is that they were turned away from truth and turned toward falsehood.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 56–57:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: "You have certainly remained within the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware"﴾ (30:56).

Qatadah used to say: "This is of the advanced (al-muqaddam) which means the delayed (al-ta'khir)."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: "You have certainly remained within the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection"﴾. He said: "This is from the inversions of speech (maqadim al-kalam). Its interpretation is: 'And those who were given faith and knowledge will say: You have certainly remained within the Book of God'"[[In Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani (4: 224), al-Wahidi said: "The exegetes have interpreted this as inversion and postponement, with the implied meaning: 'And those who were given knowledge will say: [you remained] in the Book of God.' This differs from what Qatadah stipulated in his report which the author narrates here."]].

It is mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he used to say: The meaning of that is: "And those who were given knowledge of the Book of God, and faith in God and His Book, will say."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿in the Book of God﴾:

It means: in what God wrote, of what had preceded in His knowledge, that you would remain in it. ﴿So this is the Day of Resurrection﴾ means: this is the day on which people are raised from their graves. ﴿But you were not aware﴾ means: but you were not aware in the world that it would occur, and that you would be resurrected after death; therefore you used to deny it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So on that Day, those who did wrong will not benefit from their excuse, nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾ (30:57).

The Exalted says: On the Day when they are raised from their graves, ﴿those who did wrong will not benefit from their excuse﴾, meaning: those who denied the Resurrection in the world, ﴿their excuse﴾, which is their saying: "We did not know that it would occur, nor that we would be raised." ﴿Nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾ means: nor will these wrongdoers be returned, on that Day, from what they used to deny in the world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 30, verses 58–60:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example. But if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, "You are but falsifiers."﴾ (58)

His exalted remembrance says: And We have certainly presented for mankind in this Qur'an every kind of example, as proof against them and as a reminder to them of the oneness of God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And if you bring them a sign﴾

That is: And if you, O Muhammad, bring these people a sign, meaning a proof of the truth of what you say, ﴿those who disbelieve will surely say, "You are but falsifiers."﴾ That is: those who denied your message and rejected your prophethood will surely say, "You who confirm Muhammad in what he has brought you are nothing but falsifiers in what you bring us of these matters."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾ (59)

His exalted remembrance says: Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know the reality of what you, O Muhammad, bring them from God of these lessons, admonitions and clear signs, so they do not comprehend the proof from God, nor understand from Him what He recites to them of the verses of His Book. Therefore, in their transgression, they wander about in confusion.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾ (60)

His exalted remembrance says: So be patient, O Muhammad, over what harm reaches you from them, and convey to them the message of your Lord. Indeed, the promise of God that He made to you of victory over them, triumph against them, and the establishment of you and your companions and followers upon the earth, is true. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾ That is: let not the forbearance and opinion of you be swayed by these polytheists who do not have certainty about the Hereafter and do not believe in resurrection after death, so that they hinder you from the command of God and from carrying out what He has charged you with, namely conveying His message.

* *

⁕ Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah, that a man from the Kharijites recited behind Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿Indeed, if you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers﴾, and Ali said: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

⁕ He said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Uthman ibn Abi Zur'ah, from Ali ibn Rabi'ah, who said: A man from the Kharijites called out to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) while he was in the dawn prayer, saying: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: if you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers﴾. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) answered him while he was in the prayer: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾. He said: A man from the Kharijites behind Ali in the morning prayer said: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: if you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers﴾. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) listened to him attentively until he understood what he said, then answered him while in the prayer: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rum.
